拼湊某人最不堪的時刻
"Critics said netizens had stitched together the teenager's worst moments from unrelated incidents."
6 follow someone indefinitely
永遠跟隨某人
"A permanent digital record can follow someone indefinitely long after an incident is forgotten."
7 a loss of emotional control
情緒失控
"Repeated public outbursts may reflect a loss of emotional control rather than simple rudeness."
8 an inadequate store policy
店舖政策不完善
"Some blamed an inadequate store policy on delayed orders for triggering the confrontation in the first place."
9 convict based on partial footage
單憑片面片段定罪
"Viewers often convict based on partial footage before any official account of events emerges."
10 a pattern of public outbursts
公開發怒的規律
"Three unrelated clips together suggested a pattern of public outbursts rather than a single lapse."

🪜 Mainland Social Media Users Slam Hongkongers' 'Outdated' Escalator Habit

Social Trend·4 Oct 2026
English

A post on the mainland platform Xiaohongshu complaining that Hongkongers queue single-file on one side of MTR escalators, rather than standing on both sides, has reignited a long-running debatecaused an old argument to flare up again after a period of calm再次引發長期爭論 about the city's "left walk, right stand" habit. The user argued the practice is outdated and halves an escalator's carrying capacitycuts the maximum number of people an escalator can move in half令扶手電梯運載量減半, prompting thousands of comments that quickly polarised into two entrenched campssplit sharply into two firmly opposed groups分裂成兩個對立陣營 defending or attacking the custom.

Supporters say leaving the left side free helps commuters in a hurry and doubles as an emergency escape routea path kept open specifically for people to leave quickly if something goes wrong緊急逃生通道, framing the habit as a safeguard rather than an inefficiency. Critics point to official guidance from the MTR and the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department, which has long urged passengers to hold the handrail and stand still on both sides, and to safety datastatistics or figures collected specifically about how safe or unsafe something is安全數據 showing 233 escalator accidents in the first half of this year alone, many involving elderly passengers who lost their balance while walking. The clash has since widened into a broader cross-border spata minor quarrel between people from different sides of a border跨境小爭執 over which city's commuting norms deserve to be called sensible.

中文翻譯

內地社交平台小紅書一名用戶日前投訴,指港鐵扶手電梯乘客只習慣企定一邊排長龍,而非兩邊都站立,令話題再次引發長期爭論,觸及香港「左行右立」的老習慣。該網民認為這種做法已經過時,令扶手電梯運載量減半,帖文引來數千則留言,迅速分裂成兩個對立陣營,有人力撐、有人力批。

支持者認為,預留左側通道方便趕時間的乘客,亦可充當緊急逃生通道,將這種習慣定性為一種保障而非低效率;反對者則引用港鐵及機電工程署一直以來的指引,要求乘客緊握扶手並於兩邊站穩,並引用安全數據,指今年上半年已錄得233宗扶手電梯意外,當中不少涉及在電梯上行走而失平衡的長者。這場爭論自此擴大成一場跨境小爭執,爭論哪個城市的乘車習慣才稱得上合理。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Cross-border perception gap over local habits 跨境認知差距下的本地習慣
    Mainland visitors and Hongkongers often read the same behaviour differently: what locals see as courteous queuing, outsiders see as inefficient. The clash reveals how quickly a routine civic habit becomes a flashpoint for mutual stereotyping once it crosses the border onto a shared platform.
    內地旅客與香港人對同一種行為,往往有截然不同的解讀:本地人視之為有禮的排隊方式,外人卻視為低效率。這場爭論揭示,一個尋常的公民習慣,一旦跨境並登上共用的網絡平台,便可以多迅速演變成互相標籤化的爆發點。
  • Elderly safety risk from walking on escalators 長者在電梯上行走的安全風險
    MTR data showing half of escalator injuries involve elderly passengers suggests the 'walk left' habit is not merely inefficient but genuinely dangerous for an ageing population. Safety campaigns may need to target this group specifically rather than appeal to commuters in general.
    港鐵數據顯示,一半的扶手電梯意外涉及長者乘客,反映「左行」習慣不僅低效,對人口老化的社會而言更屬真正危險。安全宣傳或許需要特別針對這個群組,而非籠統地向所有乘客宣傳。
  • Government guidance versus ingrained public habit 官方指引與根深蒂固的公眾習慣
    Official advice to stand on both sides has existed for years without changing behaviour, exposing the limits of safety campaigns that rely on signage and announcements alone. The episode raises the question of whether regulators should consider firmer measures, such as physical barriers or escalator redesign, rather than repeating advice the public has learned to ignore.
    官方多年來一直建議乘客於兩側站立,卻始終未能改變行為,揭示單靠告示牌及廣播的安全宣傳成效有限。事件引發一個問題:監管機構應否考慮更強硬的措施,例如設置實體圍欄或重新設計電梯,而非一再重複公眾早已學會視若無睹的勸告。
  • Why efficiency obsession misses the point 過度追求效率忽略了重點
    Treating escalator etiquette purely as an efficiency problem overlooks why many Hongkongers defend the habit: it preserves a clear lane for people in genuine need of speed, such as those late for work or facing a medical emergency. A marginal efficiency gain may not be worth sacrificing a safeguard that benefits a smaller, more urgent group of users.
    純粹將電梯禮儀視為效率問題,忽略了許多香港人堅持這種習慣的原因:它為真正需要趕路的人,例如遲到上班或面對醫療緊急情況的乘客,保留一條暢通的通道。為一項微不足道的效率提升,犧牲一項惠及人數較少但情況更緊急的使用者的保障,或許並不值得。

💨 Hongkongers Clash Over Ear-Piercing Portable Fan Noise

Social Trend·3 Oct 2026
English

A seemingly trivial gripe about handheld fans has snowballedgrew rapidly from a small issue into something much bigger滾雪球般擴大 into one of Threads' most heated debates this week, after Hong Kong commuters began swapping stories of being trapped beside strangers blasting piercingsharp, high-pitched and uncomfortable to hear刺耳的 fan noise on packed buses and trains. One widely shared post, in which a passenger was filmed confronting a fan-wielding commuter, racked up tens of thousands of views and ignited a sprawling thread of agreement and backlash that quickly spiralled into a referendum on basic mannersa situation treated as if it were a public vote on what counts as good behaviour變相公投 in cramped public spaces.

Some networks called for legislation cappingsetting an upper limit on something設定上限 fan decibel levels in enclosed public spaces, arguing that a clear legal threshold would settle the dispute once and for all, while others accused critics of policing other people's basic comfortexcessively controlling or criticising how other people seek comfort過度管束他人的基本舒適 in a city already short on breathing room. The row has since splintered into smaller skirmishes over etiquettesmall, repeated disputes about socially acceptable behaviour禮儀上的零星爭執, with commuters trading competing claims about who has the greater right to comfort when private habits collide with shared space.

中文翻譯

一宗看似微不足道、關於手提風扇的小爭拗,本星期在Threads滾雪球般擴大,成為最熾熱的話題之一,事緣有香港乘客開始分享自己被困在擠迫巴士及列車上,被陌生人開著的刺耳風扇聲音「夾擊」的經歷。其中一則廣傳帖文,拍到一名乘客與開著風扇的乘客當場理論,瀏覽量高達數萬,並掀起一連串支持與反對的龐大討論,迅速演變成一場關於密閉公共空間基本禮儀的變相公投。

有網民要求就密閉公共空間的風扇噪音訂立分貝上限的法例,認為明確的法律門檻能一次過解決爭議;亦有人反駁批評者是在一個本已擁擠不堪的城市裡,過度管束他人的基本舒適。這場爭論自此分裂成多場較小的禮儀上的零星爭執,乘客紛紛爭論,當個人習慣與公共空間相衝時,究竟誰更有權享有舒適。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Noise etiquette on crowded public transport 擠迫公共交通上的噪音禮儀
    As Hong Kong's MTR carriages and buses grow ever more crowded, even a small personal device can intrude on dozens of strangers at once. The portable fan row reveals how shared, confined spaces amplify minor irritations into full-blown disputes, testing whether commuters can agree on unwritten rules of consideration when private comfort collides with communal space.
    隨着港鐵車廂及巴士日益擁擠,即使一件細小的個人用品,亦足以同時打擾數十名陌生人。這場手提風扇爭議揭示,共享而狹窄的空間如何將微小的煩擾放大成全面爭拗,考驗乘客能否在私人舒適與公共空間相衝之際,就約定俗成的體諒規則達成共識。
  • Calls to legislate against handheld fan noise 要求就手提風扇噪音立法
    Frustrated commuters have urged lawmakers to set decibel limits on portable fans, much as noise ordinances already govern construction and nightlife. Critics counter that legislating against such a minor, everyday object risks trivialising the Legislative Council's time and raises thorny questions about how authorities would even enforce such a rule on a moving bus.
    感到不滿的乘客已促請立法者,為手提風扇訂立分貝上限,猶如現有噪音條例規管建築工程及夜生活場所一樣。批評者則反駁,就這種微小的日常用品立法,恐令立法會的時間顯得兒戲,亦引發當局如何在行駛中的巴士上執行這種規例的棘手問題。
  • Physiological need versus shared-space comfort 生理需要與共享空間舒適的角力
    Defenders of noisy fan users argue that the backlash overlooks genuine physical discomfort: outdoor labourers, the elderly and those prone to overheating may rely on a fan as a basic necessity rather than a luxury. This counter-view challenges the assumption that quietness should always trump a person's immediate bodily comfort in public.
    為開著風扇的乘客辯護的人認為,這場反彈忽略了真正的身體不適:戶外勞工、長者及容易過熱的人士,或許視風扇為基本需要而非奢侈品。這種反論質疑,寧靜是否應該永遠優先於個人在公共場所即時的身體舒適。
  • Judging strangers by the sound of their habits 單憑聲音判斷陌生人的習慣
    Underlying the dispute is an unspoken judgment about who gets to feel entitled to comfort in public: critics note that fan users are often assumed to be inconsiderate without regard for their circumstances, exposing how quickly online strangers leap to class-tinged assumptions about manners, upbringing and who truly belongs in a civilised public space.
    這場爭議背後,隱藏着一種未經言明的判斷——誰才有資格在公共場所享有舒適。批評者指出,開風扇的乘客往往被假設為不懂體諒,而不問其背後原因,這揭示網上陌生人何其迅速,便對他人的禮儀、教養,以及誰才真正屬於一個文明的公共空間,作出帶階級色彩的判斷。

🧵 Why Threads is quietly taking over Hong Kong teens' feeds

Social Trend·2 Oct 2026
English

Meta's text-based platform Threads has quietly become one of the fastest-growing social apps among Hong Kong youth, with awareness among local users climbing from 36 percent shortly after its 2023 launch to 66 percent more recently, while active usage has roughly tripled over the same period. The 18-to-34 age group is driving most of this growth, gravitating towardsbeing naturally attracted or drawn towards something自然地傾向於 the platform's fast-moving, text-first format for real-time commentary on everything from celebrity gossip to breaking local news, a shift that has quietly chipped away atgradually reduced something bit by bit逐步削弱 rival apps' share of daily attention.

Much of the appeal lies in Threads' seamless integrationthe combination of two things so smoothly that they work as one without friction無縫整合 with Instagram, which most Hongkongers already use — joining Threads requires little more than a single tap, instantly carrying over an existing network of followers. This frictionless onboardinga process of joining or starting to use something that involves no obstacles or difficulty零阻力加入流程, combined with video content increasingly permeatingspreading through and becoming a noticeable part of something滲透;瀰漫 the platform, has made it an attractive alternative to more saturated apps, even as sceptics wonder whether the surge in sign-upsa sudden sharp increase in the number of people registering for something註冊人數急增 reflects curiosity more than lasting loyalty.

中文翻譯

Meta旗下以文字為主的社交平台Threads,已悄然成為香港青少年之間增長最快的社交應用程式之一。本地用戶的認知度由2023年平台推出後不久的百分之三十六,攀升至近期的百分之六十六,同期活躍使用人數亦大約增長三倍。帶動這股增長的主要是十八至三十四歲的年齡層,他們自然地傾向於這個節奏明快、以文字為主的平台,用作即時評論,內容涵蓋明星八卦以至本地即時新聞,這股轉向更悄悄逐步削弱了其他應用程式在用戶日常注意力中的份額。

Threads的吸引力,很大程度上在於它與大部分香港人已在使用的Instagram無縫整合——加入Threads只需輕輕一按,便可即時承接現有的追蹤者網絡。這種零阻力加入流程,加上平台上影片內容日漸滲透,令Threads成為在眾多已趨飽和的應用程式中,一個吸引力十足的新選擇,即使有懷疑者質疑,這股註冊人數急增的現象,反映的或許只是好奇心,而非長久的忠誠度。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Platform migration driven by network portability 由網絡可攜性驅動的平台轉移
    Because joining Threads instantly carries over an existing Instagram follower list, users face almost no cost in switching attention to a new app, showing how platform design, not just content quality, can determine which networks succeed in capturing youth attention.
    由於加入Threads即可即時承接現有Instagram的追蹤者名單,用戶幾乎毋須付出任何代價,便能將注意力轉移至新平台,反映平台設計本身,而非單靠內容質素,足以決定哪個網絡能成功吸引年輕用戶的注意力。
  • Text-first format rewards fast local commentary 以文字為先的格式獎勵快速本地評論
    Unlike video-heavy apps that demand editing and production effort, Threads' text format lets users react to breaking local news or celebrity gossip within seconds, making it especially suited to the rapid, low-effort commentary culture favoured by younger users across Hong Kong.
    與需要剪接及製作心力的影片平台不同,Threads以文字為主的格式,讓用戶能在數秒內對本地即時新聞或明星八卦作出反應,因此特別適合香港年輕用戶偏好的那種快速、低投入的評論文化。
  • Fragmenting attention across too many apps 注意力分散於過多應用程式之間
    As Hong Kong teenagers now split their time between Instagram, TikTok, Threads and other apps, schools and parents face growing difficulty monitoring where sensitive conversations actually happen, complicating efforts to teach responsible online behaviour across an increasingly scattered social media landscape.
    隨着香港青少年將時間分散於Instagram、TikTok、Threads及其他應用程式之間,學校及家長要監察敏感對話實際發生在哪個平台亦愈見困難,令在日益分散的社交媒體生態中,教導負責任上網行為的工作更形複雜。
  • Is Threads' growth actually meaningful engagement? Threads的增長,是否真正代表有意義的參與?
    A counter-argument questions whether rising awareness and sign-ups reflect genuine engagement or simply passive app-hopping encouraged by one-tap migration, since many new accounts may lie dormant, making usage statistics a weaker indicator of real cultural influence than they first appear.
    另一種反論質疑,認知度及註冊人數上升,是否真正反映用戶的積極參與,抑或僅僅是「一按即轉」機制所鼓勵的被動式轉換應用程式行為,畢竟許多新帳戶可能處於閒置狀態,令使用數據作為真實文化影響力指標時,其說服力比表面看來更弱。

"Users could port over an existing network of followers with a single tap when joining the app."

🧸 Labubu blind-box craze keeps collectors hooked

Social Trend·1 Oct 2026
English

The 'Labubu' craze, centred on Pop Mart's mischievous, pointy-toothed collectible figures, continues to dominate feeds on Instagram and TikTok among Hong Kong youth. Designed by Hong Kong-raised artist Kasing Lung, the "ugly-cute" monster is typically sold in blind boxespackaging that hides which specific item is inside until opened盲盒, meaning buyers only discover which figure they have bought after tearing open the packaging, a mechanic that has proven highly addictivecausing a strong, often harmful urge to repeat an activity令人上癮的 and keeps shoppers returning for one more box in the hope of landing a rare pullsucceeding in obtaining an uncommon item through random chance抽中罕見款.

Celebrity endorsements, including from K-pop and Hollywood stars spotted with the dolls clipped to designer handbags, have lent the toy an aura of must-have glamouran impression of being highly desirable that makes people feel they need to own it令人非買不可的光環 that goes well beyond its humble price tag. Resale prices for rare editions can soar well above retail valuerise dramatically higher than the original selling price遠超原價飆升, prompting overnight queueslines of people waiting, sometimes through the night, for something to go on sale通宵排隊 outside stores and heated online bidding wars. For many Hong Kong teenagers, collecting and trading Labubu figures has become a social ritual, compared constantly across social media and increasingly treated as a currency of tastesomething used informally to measure or display a person's style or social status品味的象徵資本 in its own right.

中文翻譯

以泡泡瑪特頑皮尖牙收藏玩偶為中心的「Labubu」熱潮,持續佔據香港青少年在Instagram及TikTok上的動態消息。這款「醜萌」怪獸由在香港成長的藝術家龍家昇設計,一般以盲盒形式發售,意即買家必須拆開包裝後,才能得知自己抽中哪一款公仔——這種銷售機制已證實極易令人上癮,令買家一再購買,只為抽中罕見款。

包括K-pop及荷里活明星在內的名人紛紛將玩偶扣在名牌手袋上,為這款玩具添上一種令人非買不可的光環,遠超其原本平實的價錢所能解釋。罕見版本的轉售價格有時遠超原價飆升,促使店外出現通宵排隊,網上競投亦十分熾熱。對不少香港青少年而言,收集及交易Labubu公仔已成為一種社交儀式,他們不斷在社交媒體上互相比較,更漸漸視之為一種品味的象徵資本。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Celebrity endorsement as a trust shortcut 名人代言成為信任捷徑
    When K-pop idols and Hollywood stars are seen with the same figures clipped to designer bags, fans borrow the celebrity's perceived taste and status, treating endorsement as a shortcut to deciding what is worth owning rather than judging the toy on its own merits.
    當K-pop偶像及荷里活明星被拍到將同款玩偶扣在名牌手袋上,粉絲便借用該名人看似具備的品味與地位,將名人代言視為判斷何者值得擁有的捷徑,而非單憑玩具本身的價值作出判斷。
  • Trading rituals build teenage social bonds 交易儀式建立青少年社交連繫
    Comparing, swapping and negotiating figures with classmates gives Hong Kong teenagers a shared activity and vocabulary, similar to earlier generations trading cards or stickers, suggesting the craze functions less as consumerism and more as a structured form of peer bonding.
    與同學比較、交換及議價玩偶,為香港青少年提供了一項共同活動及共通語言,類似上一代交換卡牌或貼紙的玩法,反映這股熱潮與其說是消費主義,倒更似一種有組織的同輩聯繫方式。
  • Queuing culture and real-world safety risk 排隊文化與現實安全隱憂
    Long queues outside stores for restocks have occasionally led to crowding, pushing and disputes among buyers desperate not to miss a release, raising practical safety concerns that retailers have been slow to manage through better queue management or online allocation systems.
    店外為補貨而排起的長龍,偶爾引發人群擁擠、推撞甚至爭執,因為買家都急於不想錯過發售,此情況帶出實際的安全隱憂,而零售商在改善排隊管理或網上分配制度方面,反應一直緩慢。
  • A fad that teaches poor financial habits 助長不良理財習慣的潮流
    A counter-argument holds that normalising repeated blind-box purchases and reselling at a markup teaches teenagers to treat gambling-like spending as ordinary leisure, quietly embedding habits of impulsive, chance-based consumption at an age when sound financial judgement is still being formed.
    另一種反論認為,將反覆購買盲盒並加價轉售的行為常態化,等同教導青少年將近似賭博的消費視為尋常娛樂,在理財判斷力尚未成熟的年紀,悄悄植入衝動且憑運氣的消費習慣。

刺激需求

競投戰

"Trading figures with classmates functions as a structured form of peer bonding rather than mere consumerism."

🧸 The Labubu Blind-Box Craze Won't Let Go

Social Trend·30 Sep 2026
English

A small, wide-eyed, sharp-toothed plush monster named Labubu has spent much of 2026 colonisingto spread through and dominate a space, used figuratively here佔據;蔓延至 feeds across TikTok, Instagram and Threads. Originally designed by Hong Kong-based artist Kasing Lung and sold by mainland retailer Pop Mart, the figure is distributed through blind boxessealed packaging that hides which specific item a buyer will receive盲盒, meaning buyers do not know which variant, common or rare, they will receive until they open the box, a mechanic that keeps collectors coming backcontinues to make buyers want to purchase again and again令收藏者一再回購 for another purchase.

Unboxing videos, styling tutorials and even authentication clipsshort videos that check whether an item is genuine rather than counterfeit驗證真偽短片, where fans scrutinise stitching and paint to weed out counterfeits, have racked up billions of views, with the toys now commonly clipped onto handbags as status-signalling accessoriesitems worn or displayed mainly to show off social status彰顯身份的配飾 among Hong Kong teenagers and young professionals alike. Resale prices for rare variants have, in some cases, balloonedincreased very rapidly to a much larger amount急劇膨脹 to many times the original retail price, turning a children's toy into a fully fledged secondary marketa market where goods are resold after their first sale二手交易市場 complete with its own grading standards and bragging rights.

中文翻譯

一隻名為Labubu、有著大眼睛和尖牙的小毛絨怪獸玩偶,在2026年大部分時間裡佔據了TikTok、Instagram及Threads的動態消息。這款玩偶最初由香港藝術家龍家昇設計,並由內地零售商泡泡瑪特(Pop Mart)發售,採用盲盒形式銷售,意即買家在拆開盒子之前,都無法得知自己將會抽中普通版還是隱藏稀有版本,這種機制令收藏者一再回購。

開箱影片、搭配造型教學,甚至驗證真偽短片——粉絲仔細檢視縫線及塗裝以辨別贗品,累積觀看次數已達數十億次,這些玩偶更成為香港青少年及年輕專業人士之間扣在手袋上、彰顯身份的配飾。部分罕見款式的轉售價格,有時急劇膨脹至原價的好幾倍,令一件兒童玩具演變成一個擁有自身評級標準及炫耀資本的成熟二手交易市場。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Collecting as a marker of belonging 收藏成為歸屬感的象徵
    Clipping a Labubu onto a handbag signals membership in a shared youth culture, and Hong Kong teenagers who display rare variants gain visible social standing among peers, turning a mass-produced toy into a personal statement of taste and group identity.
    將Labubu扣在手袋上,象徵着加入一種共同的青年文化,而展示稀有款式的香港青少年,亦藉此在同輩間獲得明顯的社會地位,令一件量產玩具變成個人品味與群體身份的宣示。
  • Resale markets and the ethics of scarcity 轉售市場與稀缺倫理
    Manufacturers deliberately limit rare variants to inflate demand, and scalpers then exploit that scarcity to resell figures at inflated prices; this raises questions about whether companies bear responsibility for designing products around compulsive, gambling-like purchasing behaviour in young, impressionable consumers.
    生產商刻意限制稀有款式的數量以刺激需求,黃牛則乘機利用這種稀缺性,將玩偶以高價轉售;此現象引發疑問——企業是否應該為設計出誘使年輕、易受影響的消費者,養成近乎賭博式強迫消費行為的產品,承擔責任。
  • Authentication culture signals market distrust 驗證文化反映市場信任危機
    The rise of dedicated 'authentication' videos reveals how counterfeit figures have become so widespread that buyers no longer trust retail packaging alone, forcing collectors to rely on community-verified expertise before trusting the legitimacy of what they have actually purchased online.
    專門的「驗證真偽」影片興起,反映冒牌玩偶已氾濫到買家不再單靠零售包裝便能信任的程度,迫使收藏者須依賴社群認證的專業知識,才能相信自己網上購得的物品確實正貨。
  • Is the craze simply manufactured hype? 這股熱潮只是人為炒作?
    Sceptics argue that blind-box toys manufacture artificial scarcity, while algorithm-driven unboxing content manufactures desire itself, suggesting the craze reveals far more about effective marketing design than about any genuine artistic merit or lasting collectible value in the figures themselves.
    質疑者認為,盲盒玩具製造的是人為稀缺,而演算法主導的開箱內容,製造的則是慾望本身,這反映這股熱潮更多說明的是有效的市場營銷設計,而非玩偶本身真正具備的藝術價值或長久收藏意義。

🥤 The Viral 'Hong Kong Sprite Iced Tea' Recipe Sweeping Social Media

Social Trend·28 Sep 2026
English

A deceptively simple drink has taken TikTok and Instagram by storm: the 'Hong Kong Sprite Iced Tea', made by steeping black tea bags directly inside a bottle of Sprite before adding ice and a slice of fresh lemon. Searches for the recipe have surgedincreased suddenly and sharply急升 by over 200 percent, and the trend has proven so lucrative that a soft drinks manufacturer moved quickly to capitalise on the crazetake advantage of a sudden popular trend to gain profit趁熱潮獲利, launching 'Spritea', a bottled version of the fizzy, tea-infused concoctiona mixture of various ingredients混合飲品, in both mainland China and Hong Kong. Commentators note that the drink's viral appeal lies in its novelty and accessibilitythe qualities of being new and easy to obtain or do新穎性與易得性, requiring no specialist equipment and drawing on ingredients already sitting in most household fridges.

For many overseas creators, the trend has also sparked curiosity about Hong Kong's distinctive tea culture, transforming a humble local recipe into a piece of the city's soft-power exporta cultural product that enhances a place's international influence軟實力輸出. What began as an improvised kitchen hacka quick, makeshift trick invented at home without formal planning家常急就章妙法 has, almost by accident, done more to showcase local flavour abroad than any official tourism campaign, prompting some to ask whether a viral drink can really carry the weight of representing an entire culture.

中文翻譯

一款看似簡單的飲品近日席捲TikTok及Instagram——「香港雪碧凍檸茶」的做法,是將紅茶包直接浸泡在一瓶雪碧之中,再加入冰塊和新鮮檸檬片。該食譜的搜尋量急升超過二百個百分點,商機之大更促使一間汽水生產商趁熱潮獲利,迅速推出「Spritea」樽裝版本,在中國內地及香港同步發售這款汽水與茶混合而成的飲品。評論指出,這款飲品的爆紅魅力在於其新穎性與易得性,毋須任何專門工具,所用材料亦是大部分家庭雪惃早已具備的。

對不少海外創作者而言,這股熱潮亦引發他們對香港獨特茶文化的好奇心,令一道平凡的本地食譜搖身一變,成為這座城市軟實力輸出的一部分。一個原本只是家常急就章妙法的點子,幾乎無意之間,比任何官方旅遊宣傳都更能向海外展示本地風味,亦令人質疑一杯爆紅飲品,是否真能承載代表整個文化的重量。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Grassroots recipe turned branded product 民間食譜變身品牌商品
    A kitchen-table experiment with two household items became lucrative enough that a manufacturer bottled it for sale across two markets, illustrating how quickly informal online creativity can be absorbed, packaged and resold back to the very consumers who invented it.
    一個僅用兩種家常材料做成的廚房實驗,竟然商機龐大,促使生產商將其製成樽裝產品,在兩個市場同步發售;此例說明,非正式的網絡創意,可以如何迅速被吸納、包裝,再轉售給當初發明它的消費者本身。
  • Hong Kong identity carried through everyday taste 日常味道承載香港身份
    Overseas creators framed the drink as a window into Hong Kong's tea culture, turning an improvised mixture into a symbol of local identity; the city's food heritage now spreads internationally through casual recipes rather than official cultural campaigns or tourism board promotion efforts.
    海外創作者將這款飲品視為窺探香港茶文化的窗口,令一種臨時調配的飲品,搖身成為本地身份的象徵;這座城市的飲食傳承,如今透過一道隨意的食譜向國際傳播,而非依賴官方文化宣傳或旅遊局的推廣工作。
  • Low barrier to participation drives reach 低參與門檻帶動傳播力
    Because the recipe needs no specialist equipment and uses ingredients already in most kitchens, almost anyone can replicate and film it, which lowers the threshold for participation and lets the trend multiply far faster than content requiring skill or cost.
    由於這道食譜毋須任何專門工具,所用材料大部分廚房亦已具備,幾乎任何人都能複製並拍片分享,這降低了參與門檻,亦令這股熱潮的傳播速度,遠超需要技巧或成本的內容。
  • Does a drink really represent a culture? 一杯飲品真能代表一種文化?
    Critics might reasonably ask whether a viral mixing trend invented largely by overseas creators can meaningfully represent Hong Kong's tea culture at all, or whether branding it as cultural soft power overstates the significance of what is essentially a novelty drink hack.
    論者或許有理由質疑,一股主要由海外創作者發明的混飲熱潮,究竟能否真正代表香港茶文化,抑或將其包裝成「文化軟實力」,只是誇大了這種本質上屬於新奇飲品小妙法的意義。

👑 Disney Princesses' 'Pop Star' Dance Moves Spark Online Debate at Hong Kong Disneyland

Social Trend·27 Sep 2026
English

A short clip from Hong Kong Disneyland has triggered a wave of polarised reactionsstrongly divided opinions, with people taking opposing sides兩極化的反應 online after several Disney princesses swapped their familiar ballroom waltz for a beat-driven, contemporary routinea modern dance style closely timed to a song's rhythm貼合節拍的現代舞步 set to a pop song. Fan accounts on TikTok and Instagram pushed the footage to viral status within hours, and the disagreement soon hardened into something closer to a full-blown culture clasha serious conflict between groups with very different values or tastes全面的文化衝突 between generations of park-goers. Supporters praised the fresh energy, arguing that updating decades-old choreography keeps a tired stage show watchable, while detractors complained that the modern moves break the fairytale illusionspoil the sense that something magical or fictional is real打破童話幻想 long associated with the characters, turning a magical performance into something that merely copies a music video.

Comments ranged from enthusiastic ('so much fun!') to disapproving ('this is not fairytale'), and the row spread well beyond Hong Kong once international Disney fan outlets picked up the footage. The episode has become a small but telling case study in brand stewardshipthe responsible management and protection of a brand's identity品牌管理, exposing how theme parks weigh the commercial pull of staying currentthe business pressure to keep something relevant and appealing to today's audience追趕潮流的商業壓力 against the loyalty of long-time audiences who expect continuity over novelty.

中文翻譯

香港迪士尼樂園一段短片在網上引發兩極化的反應,片中幾位迪士尼公主一改以往的宮廷華爾滋舞步,跳起配合流行歌曲節奏的貼合節拍的現代舞步。多個粉絲帳號在TikTok及Instagram上載的片段在數小時內已瘋傳,爭論更逐漸演變成一場不同世代樂迷之間的全面文化衝突。支持者讚賞這種煥然一新的活力,認為更新多年未變的編舞能令表演保持可觀性;反對者則批評這種現代舞步打破了童話幻想,令原本充滿魔法感的表演淪為單純模仿音樂錄像。

網民留言反應不一,有人興奮表示「超好玩!」,亦有人不滿地說「這不是童話故事」,爭論更蔓延至香港以外地區,多個國際迪士尼粉絲媒體亦爭相報道。事件已成為品牌管理的一個小型卻具參考價值的案例,反映主題樂園如何在追趕潮流的商業壓力與長期觀眾期望延續性而非新奇感之間取得平衡。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Nostalgia versus reinvention 懷舊情懷與創新改革的對立
    Parents and older fans who grew up watching the princesses perform slow, orchestral waltzes see the new routine as a betrayal of childhood memory, while teenagers raised on short-form dance trends welcome the update, exposing how differently generations define authenticity in a beloved cultural product.
    自小觀看公主們跳着緩慢管弦華爾滋長大的父母及年長粉絲,將新舞步視為對童年記憶的背叛;而在短視頻舞蹈潮流下成長的青少年則歡迎這次更新,反映出不同世代對一件深受喜愛的文化產品,如何定義「原汁原味」有着截然不同的看法。
  • Franchise heritage meets globalised pop culture 經典傳承遇上全球化流行文化
    Disney's princesses carry decades of storytelling tradition as cultural heritage, yet theme parks now operate inside a globalised entertainment market driven by short-form video trends; the backlash shows the tension between preserving a franchise's identity and adapting to worldwide pop aesthetics.
    迪士尼公主承載着數十年敘事傳統,屬於一種文化遺產,但主題樂園現時身處一個由短視頻潮流主導的全球化娛樂市場;這次反彈正反映出保存品牌原有身份,與迎合全球流行美學之間的張力。
  • Context collapse fuels viral outrage 脫離語境助長網絡怒火
    Short clips stripped of context, a few seconds of choreography shared without explanation of when or why it was introduced, let viewers project their own assumptions onto the routine, showing how fragments of footage can inflate a minor change into disproportionate online controversy.
    被抽離語境的短片——短短幾秒的編舞片段,未附上任何背景說明,便任由觀眾將自身假設投射其中,反映片段的片面呈現,足以將一個微小的改動,渲染成與事實不成比例的網絡爭議。
  • A manufactured controversy over a minor change 小改動催生的人為爭議
    Arguably the furore says more about social media's appetite for outrage than about any real harm; a single dance routine at one park show is a trivial creative choice, and treating it as a cultural crisis exaggerates the stakes of routine entertainment updates.
    可以說,這場風波反映的更多是社交媒體對憤怒情緒的渴求,而非任何實質傷害;單一場表演中的一段舞步改動,本屬微不足道的創作決定,將其誇大為文化危機,未免言過其實。

🎢 Hong Kong Disneyland's 90s 'Feel Like Dance' Challenge Goes Viral

Social Trend·26 Sep 2026
English

A new short-form dance trend has taken hold of Hong Kong feeds this month: the “Feel Like Dance” challengea viral dance trend built around a specific song and set choreography「Feel Like Dance」挑戰, tied to Hong Kong Disneyland’s 2026 anniversary season and deliberately steeped indeeply influenced or surrounded by a particular quality or atmosphere充滿；浸染於 90s visual references, from retro outfits to grainy, VHS-style filters. Clips of families and friend groups performing the routine both inside the park’s main plaza and outside its gates have proliferatedincreased rapidly in number大量湧現；急速增多 across TikTok and Instagram, with creators competing to add their own playful embellishmentsextra decorative details added to make something more attractive or interesting修飾；花式添加, from costume changes to exaggerated facial expressions timed to the beat.

The challenge fits into a broader wave of content that harks back toreminds people of or refers to something from the past令人回想起；追溯至 an earlier era, a mood that has dominated Hong Kong youth culture online for much of this year. Rather than chasing unfamiliarnot previously known or experienced陌生的；未曾經歷的 new experiences, many participants appear drawn to reliving fond childhood associations with the park, treating the dance less as a passing novelty and more as an occasion for shared, nostalgic bonding between parents, children and old school friends.

中文翻譯

一股全新的短片舞蹈潮流本月攻陷香港社交媒體版面：「Feel Like Dance」挑戰，配合香港迪士尼樂園二零二六年度週年活動，刻意充滿九十年代視覺元素，從復古服飾到仿VHS錄影帶質感的濾鏡皆有。家庭及朋友群組在樂園主廣場內及園外大閂拍攝表演舞步的片段，在TikTok及Instagram上大量湧現，創作者更爭相加入自己的搞笑花式，包括換裝及配合節拍做出誇張表情。

這股潮流屬於令人回想起舊日時光的更廣泛內容浪潮，這種氛圍今年大部分時間主導著香港年輕人的網絡文化。他們並非追逐陌生的全新體驗，許多參加者似乎傾向重溫與樂園相關的美好童年回憶，將這段舞蹈視為一個讓父母、子女與舊同窗共享懷舊溫情的場合，而非僅僅一時新鮮的玩意。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Family Groups Choosing Shared Play Over Screens 家庭群組選擇共享玩樂多於緊盯屏幕
    Families performing choreography together inside the park represent a rare instance of a social media trend encouraging face-to-face, physical activity rather than passive scrolling, however briefly. This suggests that even algorithm-driven trends can occasionally create moments of genuine shared recreation among relatives who might otherwise be looking at separate screens.
    家庭成員一起在樂園內表演舞步，代表這股社交媒體潮流難得地鼓勵面對面、親身的活動，而非被動刷屏，即使時間短暫。這顯示即使是由演算法驅動的潮流，偶爾亦能為原本可能各自望著手機屏幕的親人，創造出真正共享娛樂的時刻。
  • A Theme Park Season Extended Through User Content 樂園活動季透過用戶內容延長生命力
    By encouraging visitors to generate endless variations of the same choreography, Hong Kong Disneyland effectively extends the lifespan and reach of its 2026 season promotion far beyond what official advertising alone could achieve. This demonstrates how theme parks increasingly rely on user-generated content as a core, cost-effective marketing strategy.
    透過鼓勵遊客不斷創作同一段舞步的各種版本，香港迪士尼樂園有效地將二零二六年度活動的宣傳壽命及觸及範圍，延長至遠超官方廣告單靠自身所能達到的程度。這顯示主題樂園日益依賴用戶生成內容，作為一項核心而具成本效益的推廣策略。
  • Every New Version Adds Pressure to Stand Out 每個新版本都增添突圍而出的壓力
    With so many competing versions of the same challenge circulating, creators face mounting pressure to add increasingly elaborate twists simply to be noticed, turning a simple nostalgic dance into something closer to a competitive performance. This dynamic reveals how quickly a lighthearted trend can escalate into subtle creative pressure.
    隨著同一挑戰的眾多競爭版本不斷湧現，創作者承受著日益沉重的壓力，需要不斷加入更繁複的花式才能被注意到，令一段原本輕鬆懷舊的舞蹈，變得近乎一場帶競爭性的表演。這一動態揭示出一股輕鬆潮流，可以多快演變成一種微妙的創作壓力。
  • Nostalgia Marketing Works Regardless of Authenticity 懷舊營銷奏效，無論其是否真誠
    One might argue it hardly matters whether the nostalgia driving this trend is genuine or carefully manufactured by the park's marketing team, since visitors still report enjoying themselves and bonding with friends and family in the process. Judging the trend purely on authenticity may miss the simpler point that participants are actually having fun.
    有人或會認為，驅動這股潮流的懷舊情懷究竟是真誠自發，還是樂園市場推廣團隊精心策劃，其實無關重要，因為遊客依然表示在過程中樂在其中，並與朋友家人建立聯繫。若純粹以真誠程度評價這股潮流，或會忽略一個更簡單的事實：參加者確實樂在其中。

🥤 Hong Kong Ice-Tea-Sprite Mix Goes Viral

Social Trend·25 Sep 2026
English

A home-mixed concoction known simply as the Hong Kong ice-tea-and-Sprite mix has been quietly dominating local feeds this week, with creators dressing upto present something in an appealing or flattering way包裝；美化呈現 the combination as a nostalgic yet refreshing reinvention ofthe act of presenting something familiar in a new form對……的重新演繹 a cha chaan teng staple. Short clips showing the mixing process, often filmed inside unassumingmodest and not drawing attention to itself毫不起眼的 local diners, have accumulated sizeable followings across TikTok and Instagram, with commenters openly sentimentalisingtreating something with exaggerated emotion or nostalgia賦予過度情感；懷舊化 an everyday order rather than chasing imported novelties from abroad.

The trend sits within a wider seasonal shift towards celebrating small, unremarkablenot special or noticeable; ordinary不起眼的；平凡的 decisions as minor personal victories, a mood already visible in several other viral formats this month. For Hong Kong youth especially, the appeal seems to lie in championingto support or promote something enthusiastically大力支持；推崇 distinctly local culture over overseas fads, treating a familiar diner order as something worth celebrating on its own terms rather than dismissing it as unworthy of notice. The clips offer a light-hearted yet telling glimpse into how identity and everyday consumption continue to intersect online.

中文翻譯

一款名為「港式凍茶溝雪碧」的自製飲品組合，本週悄悄佔據本地社交媒體版面，創作者將這款組合包裝成對經典茶餐廳點法懷舊而清新的重新演繹。展示調配過程的短片，拍攝地點多在毫不起眼的本地茶餐廳內，在TikTok及Instagram上累積了可觀的追隨者，評論者紛紛公開將這款日常點法懷舊化，而非一味追逐來自外地的新奇事物。

這股潮流屬於本季一股更廣泛的轉變，即慶祝微小、不起眼的決定為個人小勝利，這種氛圍本月已在多個其他爆紅格式中顯現。對香港年輕人而言，這股潮流的吸引力似乎在於大力推崇獨特本地文化，而非盲從海外潮流，將一款熟悉的茶餐廳點法視為值得獨立慶祝的事物，而非視之為不值一提。短片提供一個輕鬆卻具啟發性的窗口，呈現身份認同與日常消費如何持續在網絡上交織。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Choosing Local Nostalgia Over Imported Novelty 選擇本地懷舊多於外來新奇
    Unlike many viral drink trends that import a foreign gimmick, this mashup deliberately centres a cha chaan teng staple, suggesting a modest but notable preference among some young Hongkongers for celebrating home-grown food culture over chasing trends that originated overseas. This offers a small but telling counterpoint to globalised youth consumption habits.
    與許多引入外地噱頭的爆紅飲品潮流不同，這款混合飲品刻意以茶餐廳經典飲品為核心，顯示部分年輕香港人明顯傾向頌揚本土飲食文化，而非一味追逐源自海外的潮流。這為全球化的青年消費習慣，提供了一個微小卻值得留意的反例。
  • Filming Inside Diners Affects Other Customers 在茶餐廳內拍攝影響其他顧客
    Shooting mixing videos inside working cha chaan teng diners means ordinary customers trying to eat a quiet meal may end up unintentionally captured on camera or disturbed by filming equipment and repeated takes. This raises a small but real question about courtesy towards other patrons sharing the same communal space.
    在運作中的茶餐廳內拍攝調配短片，意味著只想安靜用膳的普通顧客，可能無意中被鏡頭拍下，或因拍攝器材及重複拍攝而受到干擾。這提出一個雖小卻實在的問題：在共用的公共空間內，應如何顧及其他顧客的禮貌。
  • Diners Gain Free Promotion From Viral Clips 茶餐廳因爆紅短片獲得免費宣傳
    When creators film inside specific local diners, those establishments often receive unplanned publicity and foot traffic from viewers eager to recreate the drink themselves on location. Small, family-run cha chaan teng could benefit meaningfully from this kind of organic exposure, provided owners are able to manage the resulting extra demand.
    當創作者在特定本地食肆內拍攝影片時，這些食肆往往獲得意料之外的宣傳及人流，吸引觀眾希望親身到該處重現這款飲品。只要店主能夠妥善應付隨之而來的額外需求，小本經營的家庭式茶餐廳實可從這種自然而來的曝光中實質受惠。
  • Romanticising the Ordinary Risks Seeming Contrived 將平凡事物浪漫化或顯得刻意
    Sceptics might argue that deliberately 'romanticising' an everyday drink order for content purposes feels somewhat contrived, since genuine appreciation for local culture rarely needs a camera and curated captions to exist. Framing mundane habits as a meaningful identity statement may say more about content strategy than sincere cultural pride.
    持懷疑態度者或會指出，刻意為一款日常飲品點法「浪漫化」以製作內容，顯得有點刻意，因為真誠欣賞本地文化通常不需要攝影機及經過修飾的字幕才能存在。將平凡習慣包裝成有意義的身份宣言，或許更多反映內容策略，而非真誠的文化自豪感。

🥤 Sprite + Lemon Tea: Hong Kong's Viral DIY Drink Mashup

Social Trend·24 Sep 2026
English

A homemade drink craze has been fizzing across Hong Kong’s social feeds this September, as teenagers raid supermarket shelves to concoctto make something, especially a drink or dish, by mixing various ingredients調配；混合製成 their own bespoke beverages. The standoutespecially noticeable or impressive compared with others最突出的 combination pairs Sprite with classic Hong Kong-style iced lemon tea, yielding a fizzy, citrus-forward hybrid that has spread rapidly through short recipe clips shared between friends.

Creators film themselves pouring, taste-testing and rating each attempt on camera, transforming an otherwise mundaneordinary and not interesting or exciting平凡乏味的 drink into shareable entertainment. Part of the appeal lies in how endlessly adaptablecapable of being changed or varied in countless ways可無限變化的 the format is: any two drinks can theoretically be combined, giving every creator a near-inexhaustibleimpossible to use up completely; never-ending無窮無盡的 supply of fresh content ideas. The trend reflects a wider appetite among young people for expressing individuality through small, playful acts of everyday experimentationthe process of trying new methods or combinations to see what results實驗；試驗, one short clip at a time.

中文翻譯

本月一股自製飲品熱潮在香港社交媒體上持續發酵，青少年紛紛走進超市，調配屬於自己的獨家飲品。當中最突出的組合，是將雪碧與經典港式凍檸茶混合，調配出帶氣泡與濃烈檸檬味的混合飲品，並透過朋友間流傳的簡短食譜片段迅速擴散。

創作者拍下自己在鏡頭前倒入、試味及評分每次嘗試的過程，將一杯原本平凡乏味的飲品，變成可供分享的娛樂內容。這股潮流的吸引力之一，在於這個格式可無限變化：理論上任何兩種飲品都可以互相混合，令每位創作者都擁有近乎無窮無盡的全新內容靈感來源。這股潮流反映出年輕人透過微小、富玩味的日常實驗表達個性的普遍渴望，一段短片接一段短片地呈現出來。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Pairing a Global Soda With a Local Classic 將全球汽水與本地經典配對
    Deliberately combining an international soft drink with Hong Kong-style lemon tea lets teenagers express a hybrid identity that is neither purely local nor purely global, blending the two into something distinctly their own. This small act of culinary experimentation offers a lighthearted lens on how young Hongkongers navigate belonging in a globalised city.
    刻意將一款國際汽水與港式檸檬茶混合，讓青少年表達一種既非純粹本地、亦非純粹全球化的混合身份，將兩者融合成屬於自己的獨特風味。這項小小的飲食實驗，為年輕香港人如何在一個全球化城市中尋找歸屬感，提供了一個輕鬆的觀察角度。
  • Buying Two Drinks to Make One 買兩款飲品只為調配一款
    Because the recipe requires purchasing both a soft drink and separately bought lemon tea, supermarkets and convenience stores quietly benefit from teenagers buying two items instead of one to produce a single mashed-up beverage. This shows how even a playful DIY trend can translate directly into measurable extra retail spending.
    由於這款食譜需要分別購買一瓶汽水及一瓶檸檬茶，超市及便利店因此悄悄受惠於青少年為調配一款混合飲品而購買兩件貨品。這顯示即使是富玩味的自製潮流，亦能直接轉化為實質可量度的額外零售消費。
  • Rating Culture Turns Taste Into Performance 評分文化將味覺變成表演
    Filming, tasting and publicly rating each drink combination transforms a private, casual experiment into content judged by an audience, encouraging creators to perform enthusiasm or disgust for the camera rather than simply enjoy or dislike the drink honestly. This raises questions about how authentic such reactions really are.
    拍攝、試味並公開為每款飲品組合評分，將一次私人、隨興的實驗，變成由觀眾評判的內容，促使創作者為鏡頭表演誇張的熱情或嫌惡反應，而非單純誠實地表達喜惡。這令人質疑此類反應究竟有多真實。
  • Just Teenagers Having Fun With Snacks 純粹是青少年玩味小吃
    It is reasonable to argue that mixing supermarket drinks is simply harmless teenage experimentation, no different from previous generations inventing their own snack combinations, and does not require framing as a statement about identity or consumerism. Sometimes a drink is just a drink, made for fun rather than meaning.
    有人合理地指出，混合超市飲品純粹是無害的青少年實驗，與上一代自創零食組合的玩法無異，不需被包裝成一種關於身份認同或消費文化的宣言。有時候，一杯飲品純粹只是一杯飲品，為了玩樂而調配，而非為了意義。

🛗 Hopewell Centre's Glass Lift Becomes Hong Kong's Latest Viral Sensation

Social Trend·22 Sep 2026
English

A glass observation lift tucked inside Wan Chai’s Hopewell Centre, climbing from the 17th floor all the way to the 62nd, has unexpectedly become one of the city’s most talked-aboutwidely discussed and attracting attention備受談論的 free attractions. Short clips capturing the sweeping harbour panorama as the lift glides upward have amassedgathered or accumulated in large quantities over time累積（大量） millions of views, with creators lining upstanding or waiting in a queue排隊等候 specifically to film the brief ride rather than for any other purpose inside the building.

Clips are frequently tagged alongside no-frillssimple, basic, without unnecessary extras or expense簡約、不花費的 itineraries aimed at travellers hoping to see the city without spending much, positioning the lift as a hidden gemsomething valuable or enjoyable that is not widely known未被廣泛發現的寶藏 hiding inside an ordinary commercial tower. The trend has drawn both overseas tourists and local creators keen to showcaseto display or present something in an attractive way展示 a cinematic, cost-free slice of Hong Kong life, even as the building itself remains a working office block never originally intended as a sightseeing destination.

中文翻譯

灣仔合和中心內一部由十七樓直達六十二樓的玻璃觀光升降機，意外成為全城其中一個最備受談論的免費景點。捕捉升降機上升時維港壯麗全景的短片，已累積數百萬次觀看，更有創作者特意排隊等候，只為拍攝這段短暫升降機之旅，而非為大廈內其他用途而來。

短片經常連同簡約、不花費的旅遊行程一併標籤，吸引希望毫無花費地遊覽這座城市的旅客，將升降機定位為隱藏在一座尋常商業大廈內的隱世寶藏。這股潮流同時吸引了海外旅客及本地內容創作者，爭相展示這座城市一片免費又如電影畫面般的風光，即使大廈本身仍是一座從未打算用作觀光景點的辦公大樓。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • A Free Attraction Competing With Paid Tourist Sites 免費景點與收費景點爭客
    As tourists discover they can enjoy a free, Instagram-worthy harbour view inside an office building lift, paid observation decks and ticketed attractions may lose some visitors who no longer see a reason to spend money on a similar view. This shows how viral discoveries can quietly reshape tourist spending patterns across a city.
    當旅客發現自己可以在一座辦公大樓的升降機內，免費享用猶如Instagram照片般的維港景致，部分收費觀景台及需購票的景點，或會因遊客認為無需花錢欣賞類似景觀而流失客源。這顯示爆紅發現如何悄悄重塑一座城市的旅遊消費模式。
  • Tourists Filming in a Working Office Building 旅客在運作中的辦公大樓內拍攝
    Hopewell Centre remains a functioning commercial building, and crowds of visitors queuing specifically to film the lift could disrupt staff and tenants, or create congestion that was never anticipated in the building's original design. This raises practical questions about how private commercial spaces should manage sudden, unplanned tourist attention.
    合和中心仍是一座運作中的商業大廈，而特意排隊拍攝升降機的遊客人群，可能干擾職員及租戶，或造成大廈原本設計時從未預料到的擁塞情況。這引發一個實際問題：私人商業空間應如何應對突如其來、未經計劃的旅客關注。
  • Unplanned Foot Traffic Strains Old Infrastructure 未預期人流令老舊基建承受壓力
    A lift and building designed decades ago for office workers may not have been engineered for a sustained surge of tourist traffic, raising questions about long-term wear on mechanical systems never intended to handle viral-driven visitor numbers. Sustaining the attraction responsibly may require investment the building's owners did not originally plan for.
    這座升降機及大廈設計於數十年前，原意只供辦公室員工使用，未必能承受持續湧現的旅客人流，令人質疑從未打算應付爆紅帶動訪客數量的機械系統，長遠會否承受過度磨損。要負責任地維持這項景點，或需要大廈業主當初並未規劃的投資。
  • Hidden Gems Rarely Stay Hidden or Free 隱世景點難以長久保持隱蔽或免費
    Sceptics might predict that once an unofficial attraction like this draws enough attention, management will eventually restrict access, introduce fees or limit filming, meaning the current free, spontaneous appeal is likely temporary. Viewed this way, celebrating the lift as a lasting symbol of the city may be premature.
    持懷疑態度者或會預料，一旦像這樣的非官方景點累積足夠關注，管理方最終將限制出入、收取費用或限制拍攝，意味著目前免費、隨性的吸引力可能只屬短暫。從這角度看，將這部升降機奉為城市長久象徵，或許言之過早。

Social Trend·21 Sep 2026

Record crowds have flocked to Victoria Park this Mid-Autumn Festival for the International Lantern Spectacular, and social feeds across the city have been inundatedoverwhelmed by a large quantity of something充斥；氾濫 with clips of its most photogenic exhibits. The “Feast of Light” installation, featuring oversized lanterns moulded into the shapes of egg waffles and milk tea cups, has emerged as the park’s single most covetedgreatly desired or wanted夢寐以求的 backdrop, with visitors forming long queues and patiently waiting their turn before an unobstructed shot.

Yet not everyone is convinced the rush to capture the perfect image is entirely benign. Some commentators argue that this frenzied pursuitan intense and excited rush to obtain something狂熱追逐 of a shareable photo can crowd outto push something aside through excessive demand for space or attention排擠；擠出空間 quieter, more considered appreciation of the craftsmanship behind each lantern, turning a centuries-old tradition into a brief photo opportunity before visitors move on. The episode has stirred a modest but discernibleable to be noticed or recognised clearly可察覺的 debate over whether documenting a festival for an online audience genuinely deepens cultural engagement, or merely reduces it toto simplify something complex down to a smaller, less meaningful version將……簡化為 a fleeting backdrop for personal branding.

中文翻譯

今年中秋節，維多利亞公園「國際花燈匯」吸引破紀錄人潮，而全城社交媒體版面亦充斥展覽中最具「打卡」效果的燈飾片段。以巨型雞蛋仔及奶茶杯造型燈飾為主題的「光影盛宴」裝置，已成為公園內最令人夢寐以求的拍攝背景，遊人紛紛排起長龍，耐心等候輪到自己捕捉一張毫無阻擋的照片。

然而，並非人人認同這股爭相捕捉完美照片的熱潮完全無害。有評論者認為，這種狂熱追逐可供分享照片的行為，可能排擠了對每件燈飾背後手工藝較從容、較深入的欣賞，令一項流傳數百年的傳統，淪為遊人匆匆離去前的短暫拍照機會。此事引發一場溫和但可察覺的討論，關於為網絡觀眾記錄節慶，究竟是真正加深了文化參與，還是僅僅將其簡化為個人形象包裝的短暫背景。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Photogenic Design Reshapes a Traditional Festival 打卡設計重塑傳統節慶
    Lantern displays shaped like egg waffles and milk tea cups suggest organisers are now designing traditional festival installations with social media shareability in mind, rather than purely craftsmanship or symbolism. This reflects a broader shift in how heritage events adapt their visual language to remain relevant on image-driven platforms.
    造型如雞蛋仔及奶茶杯的燈飾顯示，主辦單位設計傳統節慶裝置時，現在更著重社交媒體上的「打卡」效果，而非單純的手工藝或象徵意義。這反映出傳統節慶活動的視覺語言正廣泛轉變，以在以影像主導的平台上保持吸引力。
  • Record Crowds Raise Practical Safety Concerns 破紀錄人流引發實際安全隱憂
    Record attendance combined with visitors queuing and jostling for the best camera angle increases the risk of overcrowding, particularly around narrow walkways near the most popular installations. Organisers may need stronger crowd management measures to balance public enjoyment of a beloved festival against the practical safety of large, photo-seeking crowds.
    破紀錄的入場人數，加上遊人為爭奪最佳拍攝角度而排隊及推撞，增加了人群過度擁擠的風險，尤其在最受歡迎裝置附近的狹窄通道。主辦單位或需加強人流管理措施，以在市民享受這項深受喜愛的節慶活動與大批追求拍照機會的人群的實際安全之間取得平衡。
  • Early Arrivals Get the Best Shot 早到者搶佔最佳拍攝位置
    Because the most photogenic installations draw the longest queues, visitors who can arrive early on a weekday, rather than those only free on weekends due to work or school commitments, have a far easier time capturing the shot that performs best online. This unevenly distributes who gets to participate fully in the trend.
    由於最具「打卡」效果的裝置往往排隊最長，能夠在平日提早到場的遊人，相比只能在週末抽空前往的學生或打工仔，更容易捕捉到在網上表現最佳的照片。這令潮流的參與機會分配得並不均等。
  • Photography Can Deepen Appreciation, Not Replace It 拍照或能加深欣賞，而非取代欣賞
    Rather than overshadowing genuine appreciation, taking a photograph could be seen as part of how modern visitors engage with and remember traditional craftsmanship, extending the festival's reach to those unable to attend in person. Viewed this way, documenting the event for social media complements rather than undermines authentic cultural engagement.
    與蓋過真正欣賞的說法相反，拍照也可被視為現代遊人參與及記住傳統工藝的一種方式，將節慶的影響力延伸至無法親身到場的人。從這個角度看，為社交媒體記錄活動，是補足而非削弱真誠的文化參與。

🧸 The Blind Box Collecting Craze Continues to Grip Hong Kong Youth

Social Trend·19 Sep 2026
English

Blind-box collectibles such as Pop Mart's Labubu, designed by Hong Kong artist Kasing Lung, remain one of the most persistent crazesan intense, enduring enthusiasm for something that does not quickly fade持久不衰的熱潮 among Hong Kong youth on TikTok and Instagram. Videos of fans unboxingopening a sealed package on camera to reveal its contents開箱 mystery packaging to reveal a random figure regularly attract millions of views, with the anticipation itself forming a central part of the appeal.

Many observers argue the trend endures because randomised rewardsoutcomes determined by chance rather than guaranteed in advance隨機獎勵 keep collectors engaged even after the novelty of the character itself might otherwise fade. Critics, however, warn that the format closely resembles gambling mechanicshas structural similarities to the systems that make betting or games of chance addictive與賭博機制相似, encouraging repeated purchasesbuying the same type of product again and again重複購買 in pursuit of a rare variantan uncommon version of a collectible that is harder to obtain罕有版本.

中文翻譯

諸如Pop Mart的Labubu等盲盒收藏品，由香港藝術家龍家昇設計，仍是香港青少年在TikTok及Instagram上其中一股最持久不衰的熱潮。粉絲開箱神秘包裝、揭曉隨機人偶的影片，經常吸引數百萬次觀看，而過程中的期待感本身正是其吸引力的核心所在。

不少觀察者認為，這股潮流持續不衰，是因為隨機獎勵機制能令收藏者保持投入，即使角色本身的新鮮感已經減退。然而，亦有評論者警告，這種模式與賭博機制相似，可能助長收藏者重複購買，以追求罕有版本。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Gambling Mechanics Marketed to Minors 向未成年人推銷的賭博式機制
    Because blind boxes conceal their contents until purchase, the format mirrors gambling's reward structure closely enough to raise genuine concern when the primary audience includes secondary school students with limited financial experience. Regulators and schools might reasonably ask whether such products should carry clearer warnings about their psychological pull.
    由於盲盒在購買前隱藏內容，其獎勵結構與賭博相似程度足以引起真正關注，尤其當主要客群包括財務經驗有限的中學生。監管機構及學校或有理由詢問，這類產品是否應附上更清晰的警示，說明其背後的心理吸引力。
  • Pocket Money Spent Chasing Rare Figures 零用錢花在追逐罕有人偶上
    Students with more disposable income can afford to buy repeatedly until securing a rare variant, while those with tighter budgets are left out of the collecting status that comes with owning sought-after figures. This quietly reinforces existing inequalities in spending power among classmates, dressed up as harmless hobby collecting.
    可支配收入較多的學生，有能力不斷重複購買，直至獲得罕有版本為止，而預算較緊的學生則被排除在擁有搶手人偶所帶來的「收藏地位」之外。這種做法以無害的收藏愛好作包裝，卻悄悄加劇了同學之間消費能力上的既有不平等。
  • Packaging Waste Behind Every Mystery Figure 每個神秘人偶背後的包裝廢物
    Each blind box involves plastic figures sealed in printed boxes and additional wrapping designed to preserve the surprise, generating packaging waste disproportionate to the small toy inside. As collecting intensifies, so does the quantity of single-use plastic discarded purely to protect the element of chance that drives repeated purchases.
    每個盲盒都包含以印刷紙盒及額外包裝密封的塑膠人偶，用以保留驚喜感，產生的包裝廢物與盒內細小玩具的體積極不成比例。隨著收藏熱潮加劇，純粹為保護那種驅使人重複購買的「隨機感」而棄置的一次性塑膠，數量亦隨之增加。
  • A Hong Kong Design Success Story, Not Just a Vice 香港設計的成功故事，而非單純的惡習
    It is worth noting that Labubu was designed by a Hong Kong-born artist, meaning the craze also represents genuine creative and commercial success for local talent on a global stage. Focusing only on gambling-style criticism risks overlooking this trend's value as a rare example of Hong Kong design achieving worldwide recognition.
    值得留意的是，Labubu是由一位香港出生的藝術家設計，意味著這股熱潮同時代表本地創意及商業才能在國際舞台上取得真正成功。若只聚焦於賭博式批評，恐怕會忽略這股潮流作為香港設計贏得全球認可的罕有例子所具有的價值。

✨ The "Gold Star Behaviour" Trend Sweeps Hong Kong Youth

Social Trend·18 Sep 2026
English

A new wave of short videos under the banner of “Gold Star Behaviour”a social media trend in which creators praise themselves for small, often mundane, acts of self-discipline「金星行為」 has become popular among Hong Kong teenagers on TikTok and Instagram. Creators film themselves completing ordinary tasks, such as replying to a message promptly or drinking enough water, and reward themselves with an exaggerated celebrationa display of joy that is far greater than the occasion really warrants誇張的慶祝, often set to upbeat audio clips.

Many observers see the trend as part of a broader shift towards normalising small winstreating minor personal achievements as worthy of genuine recognition將微小成就視為正常 at a time when young people report high levels of academic and social pressure. Others, however, argue that framing basic responsibilities as noteworthy achievements may paradoxicallyin a way that seems contradictory but is nonetheless true矛盾地 reveal just how emotionally depletedlacking in the emotional energy or resilience needed to cope with daily demands情緒耗竭 many teenagers currently feel, with some describing the clips as evidence of a quiet survival modea basic state of simply coping or getting by, rather than thriving求存狀態 rather than genuine joy.

中文翻譯

一股以「金星行為」為名的短片潮流，在香港青少年之間於TikTok及Instagram上流行起來。創作者拍下自己完成日常瑣事的過程，例如及時回覆訊息或喝夠分量的水，並以誇張的慶祝方式獎勵自己，通常配上輕快的音樂片段。

不少觀察者認為，這股潮流是一種更廣泛轉變的一部分，即在許多年輕人表示承受沉重學業及社交壓力之際，將微小成就視為值得肯定的事。然而，亦有人認為，將基本責任包裝成值得注意的成就，可能矛盾地揭示出不少青少年目前情緒耗竭的程度，有人甚至形容這些短片是一種悄然的求存狀態，而非真正的喜悅。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Celebrating Survival Mode as Achievement 將求存狀態當成成就來慶祝
    Treating basic self-care tasks as worthy of celebration may reveal how depleted many teenagers feel under current academic pressure, since functioning normally has apparently become something to applaud rather than simply expect. This trend could be read less as playful content and more as a quiet signal of widespread exhaustion among students.
    將基本的自我照顧視為值得慶祝之事，或反映出不少青少年在目前學業壓力下已感到何等耗竭，因為正常地應付日常生活，似乎已變成值得鼓掌、而非理所當然的事。這股潮流與其說是玩味內容，不如說更像是學生普遍疲憊的一個悄然信號。
  • Older Generations May See This as Overindulgence 長輩或視之為過度放縱
    Parents and teachers who grew up without such validation for routine tasks may view 'Gold Star Behaviour' content as excessive self-congratulation, dismissing legitimate exhaustion as attention-seeking. This generational mismatch in interpreting the same videos can make it harder for adults to recognise when lighthearted content is masking a genuine struggle.
    成長過程中未曾因完成日常瑣事而獲得肯定的家長和老師，或會將「金星行為」內容視為過度自我讚賞，把真正的疲憊誤判為博取關注。這種對同一批短片理解上的代際差異，令成年人更難察覺輕鬆內容背後是否隱藏著真正的困擾。
  • Performing Self-Care for an Audience 為觀眾表演自我照顧
    Filming an exaggerated celebration for completing a minor task turns a private act of self-care into a performance calibrated for views and engagement, raising questions about whether such content reflects genuine emotional relief or simply mimics a format known to perform well on video platforms. Viewers may struggle to tell the two apart.
    為完成一件小事而拍下誇張的慶祝場面，將私下的自我照顧行為轉化為一場為點擊率及互動而調整的表演，令人質疑這類內容反映的究竟是真正的情緒釋懷，還是單純模仿一種已知在影片平台上容易「爆紅」的格式。觀眾往往難以分辨兩者。
  • Small Celebrations Are Harmless Self-Kindness 小小的慶祝只是無害的自我善待
    It could equally be argued that celebrating minor personal wins is simply a healthy, low-stakes form of self-encouragement, and reading deep psychological distress into every lighthearted video risks pathologising ordinary teenage humour. Some creators may genuinely just enjoy making playful content, without it reflecting any broader emotional crisis at all.
    同樣可以認為，慶祝微小的個人成就，其實只是一種健康、低風險的自我鼓勵方式，而將每段輕鬆短片都解讀成深層的心理困擾，則有將尋常的青少年幽默病態化之虞。有些創作者可能純粹享受製作玩味內容，並不代表背後存在任何更廣泛的情緒危機。

📱 Hong Kong's Gen Z underestimate how much social media fuels their loneliness

Social Trend·17 Sep 2026
English

A survey of 572 young people aged 11 to 24 by the Hong Kong Christian Service has found that Gen Z underestimatesto judge something to be smaller or less significant than it really is低估 how much social media affects their sense of loneliness. While 93.4 per cent of respondents were active social media users – starting at an average age of just 10.3 – those who used the platforms most intensivelyto a high degree; with great effort or frequency密集地 scored higher on the UCLA Loneliness Scale than non-users, averaging 20.5 points out of 40 compared with 17.7.

Researchers found that although objective scores showed heavier users were lonelier, these users often subjectivelybased on personal feelings or opinions rather than facts主觀地 felt they were not particularly isolated, with 5.8 per cent of active users found to be experiencing severe social isolationa serious lack of contact with other people嚴重社交孤立 without fully recognising it. The findings suggest that it is not social media itself but a combination of negative online experiencesharmful or upsetting interactions that occur on the internet負面網絡經歷 and diminished real-world contacta reduced amount of face-to-face interaction with other people現實社交接觸減少 that drives the trend.

中文翻譯

香港基督教服務處一項調查訪問了五百七十二名十一至二十四歲的青少年，發現Z世代低估了社交媒體對其孤獨感的影響程度。調查顯示，93.4%的受訪者是活躍的社交媒體用戶——平均初次使用年齡僅為10.3歲——而最密集使用平台的用戶，在UCLA孤獨感量表上的得分高於非用戶，平均得分為20.5分（滿分40分），相較非用戶的17.7分明顯較高。

研究人員發現，儘管客觀分數顯示重度用戶的孤獨感較高，這些用戶往往主觀上並不覺得自己特別孤立，當中有5.8%的活躍用戶被發現正經歷嚴重社交孤立，卻未完全察覺。研究結果顯示，問題的根源並非社交媒體本身，而是負面網絡經歷與現實社交接觸減少兩者結合所致。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Feeling Fine on Paper, Lonely in Practice 表面看似無事，實際卻深陷孤獨
    The gap between how isolated heavy users objectively score and how isolated they say they feel suggests many teenagers lack the vocabulary or self-awareness to recognise loneliness even as it affects them. This disconnect complicates efforts to offer timely support, since young people experiencing real distress may not identify themselves as needing help.
    重度使用者在客觀分數上顯示的孤立程度，與他們自稱感受到的孤立程度之間存在落差，顯示許多青少年可能缺乏足夠的詞彙或自我覺察能力，去辨識正影響著自己的孤獨感。這種落差令及時提供支援變得更加困難，因為真正受困擾的年輕人未必會認為自己需要幫助。
  • First Logging On at Age Ten 十歲已開始使用社交媒體
    With the average age of first social media use sitting at just 10.3, primary and early secondary schools arguably bear more responsibility for teaching healthy online habits than is currently reflected in most curricula. This finding strengthens the case for introducing structured digital wellbeing education well before students reach their teenage years.
    由於首次使用社交媒體的平均年齡僅為10.3歲，小學及初中階段理應承擔更多責任，教導健康的網絡使用習慣，而這在目前大部分課程中卻未見充分反映。這項發現有力支持在學生進入青少年階段之前，就引入有系統的數碼身心健康教育。
  • A Survey That Cannot Capture Every Young Person 一項調查未能涵蓋所有年輕人
    A sample of 572 respondents, however carefully selected, cannot fully represent Hong Kong's diverse youth population, including those without stable internet access or who rarely engage with formal surveys at all. Findings framed as representing 'Gen Z' broadly should be read with some caution about which young people were actually reached.
    即使經過仔細挑選，五百七十二名受訪者的樣本亦無法完全代表香港多元的青少年群體，當中包括缺乏穩定互聯網接入，或甚少參與正式問卷調查的青少年。因此，任何被描述為代表整個「Z世代」的調查結果，都應謹慎看待實際接觸到哪些年輕人。
  • Correlation Between Usage and Loneliness Is Not Causation 使用量與孤獨感之間只是相關，並非因果
    It is worth questioning whether heavy social media use actually causes loneliness, or whether already-lonely teenagers simply turn to platforms more often while searching for connection they are not finding elsewhere. If the latter is true, restricting screen time alone would do little to address the underlying isolation the survey identifies.
    值得深思的是，重度使用社交媒體究竟是否真正導致孤獨感，還是本已感到孤獨的青少年，只是更頻密地使用平台，試圖尋找他們在現實中找不到的連結。若屬後者，單單限制使用螢幕的時間，恐怕無法真正解決調查所揭示的潛在孤立問題。

1 underestimate an effect
低估某種影響
"Many teenagers underestimate the effect heavy social media use has on their mood."
2 loneliness scale
孤獨感量表

3 heavy user
重度使用者
"Heavy users of social media scored noticeably higher on the loneliness scale."
4 social isolation
社交孤立
"Severe social isolation can go unnoticed even by the person experiencing it."
5 self-perceived wellbeing
自我感覺的身心健康狀況
"Self-perceived wellbeing does not always match what objective measures reveal."
6 negative online interaction
負面網絡互動
"Negative online interactions appear to be a stronger predictor of loneliness than screen time alone."
7 real-world contact
現實社交接觸
"Reduced real-world contact may explain why heavy users still feel disconnected."
8 sample size
樣本數量
"A sample size of 572 cannot fully represent Hong Kong's entire youth population."
9 early exposure
早期接觸
"Early exposure to social media at age ten raises questions about digital habits in childhood."

🐉 Chinamaxxinga Gen Z internet trend of embracing and performing Chinese cultural habits and aesthetics online「中式生活風」網絡熱潮: the trend putting Chinese culture centre stage

Social Trend·16 Sep 2026
English

A viral trend known as “Chinamaxxing” has taken hold among mostly Western Gen Z users on TikTok and Instagram, who are embracingto accept and adopt something enthusiastically欣然接受 Chinese lifestyle habits — drinking hot water instead of iced coffee, wearing house slippers, and following the 養生 wellness philosophya set of beliefs about how to live healthily養生哲學 of aligning daily habits with the seasons. Influencers, including members of the Chinese diaspora, post videos on herbal remediestreatments made from plants, used in traditional medicine草本療法 and traditional skincare routines, describing themselves as entering “a very Chinese time” in their lives.

Hong Kong youth have latched ontoto become very interested in and start using something enthusiastically熱衷於；緊貼 the trend too, sharing their own takes on traditional customs and framing them as aesthetically appealingattractive or pleasing in appearance or style具美感吸引力的 lifestyle choices rather than outdated habits. The trend has sparked debate online over whether it represents genuine cultural appreciation or a form of cultural appropriationthe adoption of elements of one culture by members of another, often without understanding or proper acknowledgement文化挪用, particularly given the trend's unlikely originsa starting point that seems surprising or unexpected出乎意料的起源 among non-Chinese creators.

中文翻譯

一股名為「Chinamaxxing」的爆紅潮流，在TikTok及Instagram上以西方Z世代用戶為主興起，他們欣然接受中式生活習慣——例如飲用熱水而非凍咖啡、穿著室內拖鞋，並遵循養生哲學，將日常習慣配合四季變化調整。網絡紅人，包括海外華裔創作者，紛紛發布有關草本療法及傳統護膚習慣的短片，形容自己正進入人生中「非常中式」的階段。

香港年輕人亦熱衷於這股潮流，分享自己對傳統習俗的演繹，並將這些習慣包裝成具美感吸引力的生活方式選擇，而非過時習慣。這股潮流在網上引發熱議，爭論它究竟代表真誠的文化欣賞，還是一種文化挪用，尤其考慮到此潮流出乎意料的起源——由非華裔創作者帶起。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Traditional Habits Reframed as Global Aesthetic 傳統習慣被重新包裝成全球美學
    Practices long dismissed by some as old-fashioned, such as drinking hot water or following seasonal wellness routines, are being rebranded as desirable lifestyle aesthetics once embraced by a global audience on social media. This shows how heritage practices can gain new cultural value once filtered through international trends rather than local tradition alone.
    一些長久以來被視為過時的習慣，例如飲用熱水或遵循季節性養生習慣，一旦獲得全球社交媒體觀眾擁抱，便被重新包裝成令人嚮往的生活美學。這顯示傳統習俗一旦經過國際潮流的過濾，便可能獲得新的文化價值，而不僅僅依靠本地傳統本身。
  • Who Gets to Profit From Celebrating a Culture? 誰能從慶祝一種文化中獲利？
    Because the trend was popularised largely by non-Chinese creators rather than by Chinese communities themselves, some commentators question whether outsiders are receiving credit and attention for practices that Chinese families have followed quietly for generations. This points to a recurring ethical debate about who benefits when a culture's customs go viral.
    由於這股潮流主要由非華裔創作者而非華人社群本身帶動，有評論者質疑，外人是否因為一些華人家庭世世代代默默遵循的習俗而獲得認可及關注。這反映一個反覆出現的道德爭議：當一種文化的習俗爆紅網絡時，究竟誰才是真正的受益者。
  • Hong Kong Youth Rediscovering Familiar Customs 香港青少年重新發現熟悉的習俗
    For many Hong Kong teenagers, habits like 養生-inspired routines were simply part of family life long before the trend had a name, so participating online can feel less like adopting something foreign and more like publicly reclaiming customs they had quietly taken for granted at home.
    對許多香港青少年而言，像受養生啟發的生活習慣，早在這股潮流有名字之前，已是家庭生活的一部分，因此在網上參與這股潮流，感覺上較不像採納外來事物，更像是公開重新擁抱他們在家中一直默默視為理所當然的習俗。
  • Calling It Appropriation May Overlook Genuine Curiosity 將其一概稱為文化挪用或忽略了真誠的好奇心
    It could be argued that labelling every Western engagement with Chinese customs as appropriation discourages exactly the cross-cultural curiosity that might otherwise build genuine understanding. Not all imitation stems from mockery or exploitation, and treating sincere interest with suspicion risks making cultural exchange feel more hostile than it needs to be.
    有人或會認為，將所有西方人對中國習俗的參與一概標籤為文化挪用，恰恰會扼殺那種本可建立真正理解的跨文化好奇心。並非所有模仿都源於嘲弄或剝削，將真誠的興趣視為可疑，反而可能令文化交流顯得比實際需要更具敵意。

🧵 HK Youth Turn to Threads for 'Burnout' and Boundary-Setting Talk

Social Trend·15 Sep 2026
English

Among Hong Kong's 18-to-34 age group, a quieter social media habit has taken root: confiding into share private feelings or worries with someone, trusting them not to judge向⋯傾訴 strangers on Threads about exhaustion and the struggle to set limits at work. Awareness of the app locally has nearly tripledincreased to almost three times its original level幾近三倍增長 in under two years, and posts touching on remote work, professional identity and personal boundaries now rank among the platform's best-performing content. Rather than curated “highlight-reel” posts, users seem drawn toattracted to; interested in傾向於 raw, unpolished confessions about burnout and work-life balance.

This candidopen, honest and direct, without concealment坦率的 tone marks a departure from the glossy lifestyle content that once dominated feeds, suggesting many young Hongkongers would rather feel understood than impressed. For a generation often described as chronically overworkedsuffering from constant, long-term excessive work長期過度勞累的, publicly naming burnout appears to offer a sense of solidarity that private venting rarely provides, even as it blurs the line betweenmakes it unclear where one thing ends and another begins模糊⋯之間的界線 personal disclosure and professional risk.

中文翻譯

在香港十八至三十四歲的年齡群組中，一種較為低調的社交媒體習慣悄然形成：向Threads上的陌生人傾訴工作上的疲憊，以及難以設下界線的掙扎。本地對這個應用程式的認知在短短兩年內幾近三倍增長，而涉及遠程工作、職業身份及個人界線的帖子，現已躋身平台上表現最佳的內容之列。相較於經過精心修飾的「亮點式」帖子，用戶似乎更傾向未經修飾、坦白講述工作疲憊及工作與生活平衡的心聲。

這種坦率語氣標誌著一個轉向，脫離昔日主宰版面的光鮮生活方式內容，顯示不少年輕香港人寧願獲得理解，也不願換來讚賞。對於常被形容為長期過度勞累的一代而言，公開談論「燒盡」似乎帶來一種私下發洩難以提供的團結感，即使這模糊了個人披露與職業風險之間的界線。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Naming Burnout Breaks a Culture of Silence 公開談論「燒盡」打破沉默文化
    By openly discussing exhaustion and the need for boundaries, young Hongkongers are challenging a workplace culture that has traditionally treated overwork as something to endure quietly rather than question. This visibility could normalise seeking support earlier, before burnout escalates into more serious mental health difficulties.
    年輕香港人透過公開討論疲憊及設立界線的需要，正在挑戰一種向來將過度工作視為應默默忍受、而非質疑的職場文化。這種可見度或有助鼓勵人們在「燒盡」惡化成更嚴重的精神健康問題之前，更早尋求支援。
  • Older Colleagues May Dismiss These Conversations 年長同事或會輕視這些討論
    Senior employees who built careers on long hours and limited complaint may view boundary-setting language as entitlement rather than legitimate wellbeing concern, creating friction when younger staff bring online vocabulary about burnout into real workplace discussions. This gap in interpretation can complicate honest conversations across generations at work.
    靠長時間工作、甚少投訴而建立事業的年長員工，或會將設立界線的說法視為恃寵生驕，而非合理的身心健康關注，當年輕員工將網絡上有關「燒盡」的詞彙帶入真實職場討論時，便容易產生摩擦。這種理解上的差距，可能令跨代之間的坦誠對話變得更加複雜。
  • Sharing Workplace Struggles Under a Semi-Public Name 以半公開身分分享職場困境
    Posting candid details about one's job, employer frustrations or mental state on a platform tied to a user's real identity carries professional risk, since employers or colleagues could encounter posts never intended for them. This raises questions about how openly young workers should discuss burnout in a space that is not fully private.
    在與用戶真實身分連結的平台上，公開分享有關工作、對僱主的不滿或精神狀態的細節，本身帶有職業風險，因為僱主或同事有可能看到一些原本並非打算讓他們看見的帖子。這引發一個問題：年輕僱員應在一個並非完全私密的空間中，坦誠談論「燒盡」到甚麼程度。
  • Talking About Burnout Online Rarely Fixes It 網上談論「燒盡」鮮能真正解決問題
    A sceptic might point out that posting about exhaustion on Threads offers only temporary emotional release and public validation, without addressing the structural causes of overwork, such as understaffing or unrealistic expectations, that platform posts cannot change. Genuine improvement may require workplace reform rather than another outlet for venting online.
    持懷疑態度者可能指出，在Threads上發帖談論疲憊，只能帶來短暫的情緒釋放及公眾認同，卻無法解決造成過度工作的結構性原因，例如人手不足或不切實際的期望，而這些並非單靠帖子便能改變。真正的改善或許需要職場制度的改革，而非多一個網上發洩的渠道。

A meme known as “Jayden-mania” has taken the internet by stormspread extremely quickly and became enormously popular online在網絡上掀起熱潮 in Hong Kong since it first emerged from a video posted by two local influencers earlier this year. The clip affectionately mocksgently makes fun of something in a way that shows fondness rather than cruelty帶著親切感地取笑 a distinctive, awkward style of Cantonese-English code-switchingthe practice of alternating between two languages within the same conversation語碼轉換 often associated with certain parenting habits, built around the now-famous line “Jayden ah, mami already told you…” The phrase has since been endlessly reworked across social media, spawningcausing something new to be produced or created, often in large numbers衍生出 parody videos, merchandise and marketing campaigns that borrow its instantly recognisable rhythm.

While largely intended as light-hearted mockery, the trend has also triggered a more serious debate. Some commentators worry about its effect on children who happen to share the name Jayden, who may now face unwarranted teasingmockery that is not justified or deserved無理的取笑, while others raise concerns that the meme’s stilted phrasing could subtly normalisemake something seem standard or acceptable through repeated exposure使……變得普遍化 how younger Hongkongers mix English and Cantonese in everyday speech. Marketers, meanwhile, have swiftly woven the catchphrase into advertising aimed at younger, digitally native audiences.

中文翻譯

一個名為「Jayden-mania」的迷因，自今年初由兩位本地網絡紅人發布的短片引發以來，已在香港網絡上掀起熱潮。該短片帶著親切感地取笑一種獨特、生硬的廣東話與英語語碼轉換方式，常見於某些育兒習慣，並圍繞現已街知巷聞的一句對白：「Jayden呀，媽咪已經講過你……」。這句對白自此在社交媒體上不斷被改編，衍生出模仿短片、周邊商品，以及借用其易於辨認節奏的市場推廣活動。

雖然這股潮流大致只屬輕鬆笑料，卻亦引發更嚴肅的討論。有評論者擔心，名叫Jayden的兒童可能因此遭受無理的取笑；亦有人憂慮，迷因中生硬的說話方式，或會潛移默化地令……變得普遍化年輕香港人日常混用英語與廣東話的方式。與此同時，市場推廣人員亦迅速將這句口號編織進針對年輕、網絡原生一代的廣告之中。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Real Children Bearing the Cost of a Joke 真實兒童為一個笑話承受代價
    Although the meme targets a parenting style rather than any specific child, real children named Jayden may now face unwanted teasing linked directly to their name, an unintended consequence creators rarely consider before a clip goes viral. This highlights a recurring ethical tension between comedic intent and the real-world impact of online mockery.
    雖然這個迷因針對的是一種育兒風格，而非任何特定兒童，名叫Jayden的真實兒童卻可能因此面對與其名字直接相關的無謂取笑，而這正是創作者在片段爆紅前甚少考慮的意料之外後果。這突顯了喜劇意圖與網絡取笑在現實世界造成的影響之間，一直存在的倫理張力。
  • A Parody That Could Normalise Awkward Phrasing 一場可能令生硬說法變得普遍的模仿
    By repeating a deliberately clunky, code-mixed phrase for comic effect, the meme risks desensitising younger audiences to the very language pattern it mocks, potentially embedding stilted phrasing into everyday speech through sheer repetition. This offers a useful example of how parody and genuine linguistic influence can blur together online.
    為製造笑果而不斷重複一句刻意生硬、中英夾雜的對白，這個迷因有可能令年輕觀眾對其所嘲笑的語言模式逐漸麻木，並透過單純的重複，將生硬的說法潛移默化地植入日常用語之中。這正好說明，模仿與真正的語言影響力，在網絡上有時會變得難以分辨。
  • A Catchphrase Repackaged for Advertising 一句被重新包裝用作廣告的口號
    Marketers moved quickly to weave the meme's instantly recognisable rhythm into campaigns aimed at digitally native audiences, treating a piece of organic internet humour as a ready-made advertising hook. This reflects a broader pattern in which brands monitor viral speech patterns closely, ready to monetise them before public interest fades.
    市場推廣人員迅速將這個迷因易於辨認的節奏，編織進針對網絡原生一代的廣告活動之中，將一段自然產生的網絡幽默當作現成的宣傳噱頭。這反映出一個更廣泛的現象：品牌密切監察爆紅的說話模式，隨時準備在大眾興趣消退前將其變現。
  • Overstating the Harm of a Lighthearted Parody 誇大了一場輕鬆模仿造成的傷害
    It could be argued that commentators are reading too much significance into a brief, affectionate piece of parody that most viewers immediately recognise as exaggerated and harmless, rather than a genuine attack on any parenting style or language group. Taken too seriously, such analysis risks draining the humour out of ordinary internet culture.
    有人或會認為，評論者對一段短暫、帶善意的模仿賦予過多意義，而大多數觀眾其實一看即明白這只是誇張而無害的玩笑，並非針對任何育兒風格或語言群體的真正攻擊。若將這類分析看得過於認真，恐怕會抽走日常網絡文化本應具有的幽默感。

意料之外的後果

🎡 "Feel Like Dance" Challenge Takes Over Hong Kong Disneyland Fans

Social Trend·13 Sep 2026
English

A dance challenge tied to Hong Kong Disneyland’s anniversary celebrations, known as the “Feel Like Dance” Challenge, has taken overto become dominant or widespread very quickly攻佔 TikTok and Instagram feeds across the city, inviting fans to relive 90s dance vibes through a nostalgic, upbeat routine. Thousands of local teenagers and young adults have posted their own versions, many filmed at the park itself or re-enactedperformed again, copying an original action or event重新演繹 at home with friends.

Part of its appeal lies in how approachableeasy to engage with or attempt without special skill容易上手的 the choreography is: short, repetitive and easy to imitate, drawing in even casual users who rarely post content. Brands and influencers have swiftly capitalised on the momentumtook advantage of growing popularity to gain benefit把握聲勢, tagging the challenge to boost visibility, while Hong Kong Disneyland has amplifiedmade something stronger or more widely noticed擴大 user-generated clips through its official accounts, effectively turning ordinary visitors into unwitting brand ambassadorspeople who unintentionally promote a brand without realising it不自覺的品牌代言人.

中文翻譯

一項配合香港迪士尼樂園周年慶祝活動的舞蹈挑戰，名為「Feel Like Dance」挑戰，已攻佔全港TikTok及Instagram版面，邀請粉絲透過懷舊、節奏明快的舞步重溫九十年代舞蹈氛圍。數以千計的本地青少年及年輕人上載自己的版本，不少在樂園現場拍攝，或與朋友在家中重新演繹。

這股潮流的吸引力之一，在於舞步容易上手：簡短、重複且容易模仿，即使甚少發帖的用戶亦被吸引參與。品牌及網絡紅人迅速把握聲勢，標籤挑戰以提升曝光度，而香港迪士尼樂園亦透過官方帳戶擴大用戶生成的片段的影響力，無形中將普通遊客變成不自覺的品牌代言人。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Turning Casual Visitors Into Unpaid Promoters 將隨意遊客變成無薪推廣者
    When Hong Kong Disneyland reposts user-generated clips through its official accounts, ordinary visitors effectively become unpaid brand ambassadors, generating marketing content the park would otherwise have to produce itself. This raises questions about whether creators are adequately credited or compensated when their content is repurposed for corporate promotion.
    當香港迪士尼樂園透過官方帳戶轉載用戶生成的片段，普通遊客實際上便成為無薪的品牌代言人，為樂園製造原本需自行拍攝的宣傳內容。這引起一個疑問：當創作者的內容被挪用作企業宣傳時，他們是否獲得足夠的署名或補償。
  • Reposting Without Asking First 未經事先徵詢便轉載
    Amplifying user clips through official channels typically happens without formally seeking each creator's consent, raising a subtle privacy question about control over one's own image and likeness once content is shared publicly. Young users may not realise that posting a video effectively hands a park or brand the right to reuse it.
    官方頻道轉載用戶片段，通常並未正式徵詢每位創作者的同意，這引起一個微妙的私隱問題：內容一經公開分享後，個人應如何保有對自身形象及肖像的控制權。年輕用戶或未察覺，上載一段影片實際上等同讓樂園或品牌擁有重用該片段的權利。
  • A Dance Trend That Welcomes Non-Dancers Too 一個連非舞蹈愛好者亦能參與的舞蹈潮流
    Because the choreography demands no prior training, casual visitors who otherwise never post content can participate alongside dedicated creators, broadening who gets to take part in online culture beyond the usual pool of confident performers. This inclusiveness is one reason the format has spread so quickly beyond dedicated fan communities.
    由於這套舞步無需任何事先訓練，平常從不發帖的隨意遊客亦能與資深創作者一同參與，拓寬了能夠參與網絡文化的人群，不再局限於一向有信心表演的一群。這種包容性正是這個格式能夠迅速傳播至忠實粉絲群體以外的原因之一。
  • Manufactured Enthusiasm Driven by the Park Itself 由樂園本身主導製造的熱情
    A sceptic might suggest that the 'fan-driven' appearance of this challenge is overstated, since the park's own anniversary marketing campaign and official promotion likely did much of the work in seeding and sustaining the trend. Under this reading, what looks like organic enthusiasm may be substantially engineered from the top down.
    懷疑者或會指出，這股挑戰「由粉絲帶動」的形象被過度誇大，因為樂園自身的周年市場推廣活動及官方宣傳，很可能在播種及維持這股潮流上出了不少力。從這角度看，表面上自發的熱情，實質上或大幅由上而下地刻意營造出來。

💃 "Feel Like Dance" Challenge Sweeps Hong Kong Feeds

Social Trend·12 Sep 2026
English

A viral dance format known as the “Feel Like Dance Challenge” has taken hold ofto gain a firm and lasting influence over something牢牢佔據 Hong Kong TikTok and Instagram feeds this September, encouraging users to replicate retro choreography set against 1990s-style pop tracks, often filmed at Hong Kong Disneyland during its anniversary celebrations. Clips typically open with an ordinary, static pose before cutting to an exaggerated transformationa dramatically overstated change from one state to another誇張的轉變, a format that rewards both comic timing and genuine dance skill in equal measure.

The trend has proven especially popular among secondary school students filming with friends after school or during weekend visits to the park, with many adding captions that play upto emphasise or exaggerate something for effect刻意凸顯 the stark contrasta very obvious and striking difference between two things鮮明對比 between how differently the “before” and “after” versions of themselves appear on camera. The format has also become a vehicle for peer camaraderiefriendly feelings of trust and togetherness among a group同伴情誼, with many treating filming sessions as an informal social ritual rather than a serious performance, even as some observers note the diminishing noveltythe gradually decreasing sense of freshness or originality日漸減退的新鮮感 of yet another near-identical routine circulating online.

中文翻譯

名為「Feel Like Dance Challenge」的爆紅舞蹈格式，今年九月牢牢佔據香港TikTok及Instagram版面，鼓勵用戶重現配合九十年代流行金曲的懷舊舞步，拍攝地點多在香港迪士尼樂園周年慶祝活動現場。短片開首通常以平平無奇的靜態姿勢起手，然後突然轉為誇張的轉變，這種格式同時考驗搞笑時機及真實舞技。

這股潮流在放學後或週末到樂園遊玩的中學生之間尤其受歡迎，他們與朋友結伴拍攝，並加上字幕刻意凸顯「跳舞前」與「跳舞後」的自己在鏡頭下判若兩人的鮮明對比。這種格式亦成為同伴情誼的載體，不少人將拍攝過程視為非正式的社交儀式，而非認真的表演；即使有觀察者指出，又一條幾近相同的舞蹈短片在網上流傳，其新鮮感正日漸減退。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Before-and-After Clips and Body Image Pressure 「前後對比」短片與身體形象壓力
    Captions that poke fun at how different students look performing an exaggerated routine compared with their static starting pose risk reinforcing self-consciousness about physical appearance, even when framed as a joke. This raises a quieter concern about whether comedic before-and-after formats subtly normalise scrutinising one's own body for comic value.
    字幕取笑學生在誇張舞蹈動作與起始靜態姿勢之間判若兩人的外表，即使只是以玩笑形式呈現，也有可能強化對外貌的自我意識。這引起一個較少被談論的隱憂：這類搞笑的「前後對比」格式，是否正悄悄令人習慣以娛樂角度審視自己的身體。
  • Friendship Groups Bonding Through After-School Filming 放學後拍片凝聚友誼小圈子
    Choosing to film with friends after school or during weekend park visits turns a simple dance trend into a social ritual, giving students a shared activity and an excuse to spend unstructured time together outside formal settings. Such informal bonding may matter more to participants than the content's eventual online performance.
    選擇在放學後或週末到樂園遊玩時與朋友結伴拍片，將一個簡單的舞蹈潮流轉化為一種社交儀式，為學生提供共同活動，以及在正式場合以外自由相處的理由。這種非正式的情誼建立，對參與者而言，或許比片段最終在網上的反應更為重要。
  • Filming Time Competing With Homework Hours 拍片時間與功課時間互相競爭
    Secondary students who spend after-school hours rehearsing and reshooting a dance routine for social media are, by definition, spending less time on revision or rest, a trade-off rarely discussed openly. Teachers and parents might reasonably ask how such time commitments fit alongside existing academic and extracurricular workloads.
    中學生將放學後的時間用於綵排及重複拍攝社交媒體舞蹈短片，意味著他們勢必減少溫習或休息的時間，這種取捨卻鮮少被公開討論。老師及家長或有理由反思，這類時間投入應如何與現有的學業及課外活動負擔並存。
  • A Format Already Repeated Too Many Times 一個已經重複太多次的格式
    Given how many near-identical versions of this same challenge have already circulated across Hong Kong feeds this September, sceptics could argue the format has been thoroughly exhausted, with each new clip adding little beyond what has already been seen. This questions how much genuine attention such repetitive content still deserves.
    鑑於這個挑戰的幾近相同版本，九月以來已在香港各大版面廣泛流傳，懷疑者或會認為這個格式已被徹底用盡，每段新片段都難以帶來超越既有內容的新意。這令人質疑，這類重複性內容究竟還值得獲得多少真正的關注。
