🎷 "Saxophone Gets Louder" Meme Takes Over Hong Kong Feeds

Social Trend·11 Sep 2026
English

A global audio meme built around a saxophone riff that builds to a climaxgradually increases until reaching its most intense point漸漸推向高潮 has become one of September’s most shared formats among Hong Kong students. They apply it to everyday mishaps — an awkward encounter in a lift, a teacher catching someone mid-distraction — that suddenly feel comically dramatic once the music swells. Local meme pages have jumped on the trend, producing home-grown adaptationsversions created and adapted specifically for the local context本土改編版本 filmed on the MTR, in canteens and outside exam halls.

Part of the appeal lies in how minimalas small as possible; the least amount needed極少的 the effort required is: almost any mundane footageordinary, everyday video clips with nothing special about them平凡的片段 can be repurposed simply by adding the rising saxophone track underneath, making it one of the most accessible trends of the year. For Hong Kong teenagers navigating a new school term, the joke also functions as a collective coping mechanisma shared method people use together to deal with stress or difficulty集體應對機制, making light oftreating something serious or embarrassing as unimportant or amusing以輕鬆態度看待 the small dramas of daily student life.

中文翻譯

一段以薩克斯風旋律為基礎、逐漸推向高潮的全球音效迷因，成為九月份香港學生間最廣泛轉發的格式之一。他們將其套用於日常突發尷尬時刻——例如在電梯內的尷尬遭遇，或被老師發現分心——一旦配上愈升愈高的音樂，瞬間變得滑稽又戲劇化。本地迷因專頁亦加入戰團，製作本土改編版本，拍攝地點包括港鐵車廂、飯堂及試場外。

這股潮流的吸引力，部分在於所需付出的努力極少：幾乎任何平凡的片段只要加上逐漸升高的薩克斯風音軌，即可重新包裝，令它成為年內最易入手的潮流之一。對正迎接新學期的香港青少年而言，這個玩笑同時發揮著集體應對機制的作用，以輕鬆態度看待日常校園生活的小風波。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Localising a Global Format for Hong Kong Life 將全球格式本地化融入香港生活
    The saxophone meme began as an international audio trend but gained new meaning once local creators applied it to distinctly Hong Kong settings such as MTR carriages and exam halls. This illustrates how global digital formats are rarely adopted unchanged, but instead reshaped to reflect specific local routines and shared experiences.
    薩克斯風迷因源於國際音效潮流，但經本地創作者套用於港鐵車廂及試場等具香港特色的場景後，獲得了新的意義。這說明全球數碼格式鮮少原封不動地被採用，反而會被重新塑造，以反映特定的本地日常及共同經歷。
  • Filming Near Exam Halls Raises Classroom Concerns 在試場附近拍攝引發課堂關注
    Clips filmed outside exam halls and in canteens suggest students are willing to film and edit content during moments meant for study or rest, potentially distracting classmates nearby. Schools may need to consider whether such filming, even when harmless in intent, disrupts the focus of students preparing for assessments in the same space.
    有片段在試場外及飯堂拍攝，顯示學生願意在本應用於溫習或休息的時間內拍攝及剪輯內容，有可能令附近同學分心。學校或需考慮，這類拍攝即使出於善意，是否會干擾在同一空間準備考試的學生的專注力。
  • Turning Small Stress Into Shared Laughter 將小小壓力轉化為共同歡笑
    By exaggerating minor embarrassments into comic drama, the meme gives students a lighthearted outlet for everyday school stress, transforming awkward or tense moments into something to laugh about collectively rather than dwell on privately. This points to humour's role as an informal coping mechanism during a demanding new school term.
    透過將輕微尷尬誇張成戲劇效果，這個迷因為學生提供了應付日常校園壓力的輕鬆渠道，將尷尬或緊張的時刻轉化為集體歡笑的話題，而非獨自耿耿於懷。這反映出幽默在繁重新學期中，擔當著一種非正式應對機制的角色。
  • A Disposable Joke With No Cultural Staying Power 一個缺乏文化持久力的即棄笑話
    One could argue that a meme built entirely around a single musical sting has no inherent depth or lasting significance, and will likely vanish from feeds within weeks once a newer audio trend replaces it. Viewed this way, treating such throwaway humour as a subject worthy of serious cultural analysis risks overstating its importance.
    有人或會認為，一個完全建基於單一音效的迷因本身並無深層意義或持久價值，一旦有更新的音效潮流取而代之，很可能在數週內便從版面上消失。從這角度看，將這種即棄式幽默當作值得認真文化分析的課題，或會高估了它的重要性。

🕺 "Feel Like Dance" Challenge Sweeps Hong Kong Social Media

Social Trend·10 Sep 2026
English

A new “Feel Like Dance” challenge is sweepingspreading rapidly and widely席捲 Hong Kong TikTok and Instagram, launched alongside a Hong Kong Disneyland 2026 promotion that invites users to replicate a retro, 1990s-inspired dance routine. The format sits alongside a wider wave of “brainrot” content favoured by younger users, including the long-runningcontinuing for a great length of time without stopping長期持續的 elevator challenge and short city-walk clips filmed around Tsim Sha Tsui.

What unites these formats is their dependence onreliance on something as necessary or central依賴 repetition and exaggerated captions, deliberately crafted to be instantly recognisableable to be identified immediately without effort一看即認出的 within seconds of scrolling. For Hong Kong teenagers, joining a familiar dance format offers an effortlessrequiring little or no effort毫不費力的 way to feel part of a shared online moment, while brands increasingly latch ontoto attach oneself eagerly to something advantageous趁機搭上 such formats to reach a youth audience otherwise hard to target through conventional advertising.

中文翻譯

全新的「Feel Like Dance」挑戰正席捲香港TikTok及Instagram，配合香港迪士尼樂園二零二六年的宣傳活動推出，邀請用戶重現懷舊的九十年代舞步。這股潮流與另一波年輕用戶鍾愛的「腦腐」內容同時並存，包括持久不衰的電梯挑戰，以及在尖沙咀一帶拍攝的短片城市漫步片段。

這些格式的共通點，在於依賴重複動作及誇張字幕，刻意設計成觀眾滑動手機短短數秒內便能一看即認出。對香港青少年而言，參與一個熟悉的舞蹈格式，是一種毫不費力就能感受到共同網絡時刻的方法；而品牌亦日益趁機搭上這類格式的順風車，接觸那些難以透過傳統廣告觸及的年輕觀眾。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • When 'Brainrot' Becomes the Content Standard 當「腦腐」內容成為標準
    Pairing a nostalgic dance trend with 'brainrot' formats like endless elevator and city-walk clips suggests younger audiences increasingly reward repetitive, low-substance content over originality. Media literacy educators might ask whether such formats train attention spans for only the shortest, most predictable bursts of stimulation, at the expense of sustained engagement.
    將懷舊舞蹈潮流與「腦腐」格式（如無限重複的電梯挑戰及城市漫步短片）結合在一起，顯示年輕觀眾日益偏向獎勵重複、內容單薄的作品，而非原創性。媒體教育工作者或會質疑，這類格式是否只訓練出極短暫、可預測的刺激式專注力，而犧牲了持續投入的能力。
  • A Format Anyone Can Join, Regardless of Skill 不論技巧高低、人人皆可參與的格式
    Because the choreography is short and repetitive, the challenge requires no professional dance training or expensive equipment, letting any student participate using only a phone and a public space. This low barrier to entry means the trend spreads with unusual speed, cutting across differences in income, ability and prior social media experience.
    由於舞步簡短重複，這項挑戰無需專業舞蹈訓練或昂貴器材，只需一支電話及一個公共空間，任何學生皆可參與。這種極低的參與門檻意味著潮流能夠以驚人速度傳播，跨越收入、能力及過往社交媒體經驗的差異。
  • Brands Riding a Trend They Did Not Create 品牌搭上非自己創造的潮流順風車
    Once a dance format proves popular enough, brands routinely attach themselves to it through sponsored posts or hashtag campaigns, reaching a youth audience that typically ignores conventional advertising. This pattern of borrowing organic momentum rather than creating original content raises questions about authenticity in brand communication aimed at teenagers.
    一旦某種舞蹈格式證實夠受歡迎，品牌便會透過贊助帖子或標籤活動，慣常地將自己依附其上，藉此接觸一向對傳統廣告不聞不問的年輕觀眾。這種借助自然熱度而非創作原創內容的模式，令人質疑針對青少年的品牌傳播是否真誠。
  • Repetition Across Trends Signals Creative Stagnation 潮流間的重複反映創意停滯
    A sceptic might argue that recycling the same handful of formats, elevator challenges, city walks and now retro dance routines, shows a lack of genuine creativity among young content creators, who are simply copying whatever currently performs well. This calls into question whether such trends deserve to be treated as meaningful cultural expression at all.
    懷疑者或會指出，反覆沿用同一批格式——電梯挑戰、城市漫步，以至如今的懷舊舞步——顯示年輕內容創作者缺乏真正創意，只是不斷模仿當下流行的事物。這令人質疑這類潮流是否值得被視為具意義的文化表現。

🧋 Hongkongers dip into the viral 'Sprite Tea' trend

Social Trend·8 Sep 2026
English

A viral drink hack has taken over Hong Kong social media: dunking a tea bag straight into a bottle of Sprite. Creators on TikTok and Instagram have shown the DIY concoctiona homemade mixture people make themselves自製飲品 — typically two tea bags steeped in Sprite, then served over ice with a slice of lemon — racking upaccumulating or achieving a large amount of something累積；取得 a 200 per cent jump in related searches within a single week. The trend proved so powerful that Sprite itself capitalised on the crazetook commercial advantage of the popular trend把握熱潮, launching a ready-to-drink “Sprite Tea” product and rolling out a mobile pop-up tea stand handing out 80,000 free samples across busy Hong Kong districts.

Commentators suggest the appeal lies less in taste than in the novelty factorthe excitement of trying something new and unusual新奇感 of an unlikely, rule-breakingdefying usual conventions or expectations打破常規的 combination that is cheap, easy to replicate and instantly shareable. Even so, the speed with which a corporation moved to commercialise a grassroots recipe raises questions about how quickly authentic youth culture can be absorbed into mainstream marketingturned into part of large-scale commercial advertising被納入主流市場推廣.

中文翻譯

一種爆紅飲品製法近日主宰香港社交媒體：將茶包直接浸入雪碧樽內。TikTok及Instagram上的創作者展示這款自製飲品——通常以兩個茶包浸泡於雪碧中，加冰及一片檸檬奉上——令相關搜尋量在一星期內累積急升二百個百分點。這股潮流威力強勁，雪碧品牌亦把握熱潮，推出即飲版「Sprite Tea」，並派出流動快閂站，於多個人流密集地區派發八萬份免費試飲裝。

有評論認為，這款組合的吸引力主要不在於味道本身，而在於其出人意表的新奇感——組合方式打破常規，既便宜、又易於複製，更適合隨手分享。即使如此，企業如此迅速將一個源自草根的食譜變成商業產品，亦令人反思，原汁原味的青年文化究竟能有多快被納入主流市場推廣。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • How Fast Can a Grassroots Idea Become a Product? 草根創意能有多快變成產品？
    The near-instant turnaround from an anonymous TikTok hack to an official retail product raises questions about ownership and credit: the young creators who popularised the combination receive no compensation, while the brand captures nearly all the commercial value. This invites discussion of how intellectual contribution is recognised in viral internet culture.
    由一個匿名TikTok秘技到官方零售產品，幾乎瞬間完成的轉變，引發關於擁有權及功勞歸屬的疑問：令這款組合普及的年輕創作者沒有獲得任何報酬，而品牌卻幾乎獲取了全部商業價值。這促使人反思，在病毒式網絡文化中，智識貢獻應如何被承認。
  • Free Samples Favour Those Who Can Queue 免費試飲裝偏幫能排隊的人
    Giveaways of eighty thousand free samples sound generous, but they typically reward whoever has the free time and mobility to queue at a pop-up stand during the day, often students or those not in full-time work. This highlights how seemingly inclusive marketing promotions can quietly favour certain groups over others.
    派發八萬份免費試飲裝聽起來十分慷慨，但這類安排往往只有在日間有空閒時間及行動自由的人，例如學生或非全職工作者，才能受惠於在快閂攤檔排隊。這突顯出看似人人受惠的推廣活動，實質上可能悄悄地偏幫某些群體。
  • Single-Use Packaging Behind a Fleeting Trend 一時潮流背後的即棄包裝問題
    Tens of thousands of free samples inevitably mean tens of thousands of disposable cups, straws and bottles, generated for a trend likely to be forgotten within a season. This exposes a recurring tension between viral marketing campaigns and the environmental cost of mass-produced single-use packaging distributed purely for short-term promotional buzz.
    數萬份免費試飲裝，意味著數萬個即棄杯子、飲管及樽子，皆為一股可能在一季內便被遺忘的潮流而製造出來。這揭示了病毒式市場推廣活動，與純粹為追求短期宣傳熱潮而大規模生產即棄包裝所帶來的環境代價之間，一直存在的張力。
  • Harmless Fun Does Not Need Deeper Meaning 無傷大雅的樂趣不必有更深層意義
    It might reasonably be argued that commentators are overanalysing a simple, playful drink mashup that students enjoy purely for its taste and novelty, with no deeper commentary on youth culture or commercial ethics intended or required. Not every viral trend needs to carry symbolic weight to be worth a few minutes of enjoyment.
    亦有人合理地認為，評論者過度解讀一款學生純粹因味道及新鮮感而享受的簡單玩味飲品混搭，其中並無意圖、亦不必要帶有關於青年文化或商業道德的更深層評論。並非每一股病毒式潮流都需要承載象徵意義才值得花幾分鐘享受。

Supporters argue the update helps the park stay culturally relevantconnected to current trends and interests within a society與文化潮流相關 to a generation raised on short-form video, while critics worry it prioritises viral appeal overtreats the chance of going viral as more important than將爆紅效果置於……之上 the characters’ established identity. 中文翻譯

香港迪士尼樂園的裝扮演員在公主主題舞台環節中加入當代流行舞步，配以凌厲手部動作及TikTok式甫士，引發網上熱議。相關片段在TikTok及Instagram上迅速傳播，既獲年輕粉絲大力讚賞，亦惹來部分家長批評，認為這種風格偏離了公主角色一向溫柔、童話故事般的形象。

支持者認為這次更新有助樂園貼近文化潮流，緊貼在短片平台成長的一代；批評者則擔心這樣做把爆紅效果置於……之上角色既有形象。無論爭議如何，參與度數據顯示，這些片段確實大幅提升了樂園的網上曝光率。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Modernising a Storybook Image for a Short-Form Era 為短片時代重塑童話形象
    The shift from gentle, fairy-tale choreography to sharp TikTok-style gestures reflects a broader tension between preserving a beloved character's traditional image and adapting to the aesthetic expectations of a generation raised entirely on short-form video. This offers a clear case study in how global entertainment brands negotiate heritage against platform-driven trends.
    由溫柔的童話式編舞轉變為凌厲的TikTok式手勢，反映出在保留受喜愛角色傳統形象與迎合完全在短片文化中成長的一代的審美期望之間，存在著更廣泛的張力。這為全球娛樂品牌如何在傳承與平台主導潮流之間取得平衡，提供了一個清晰的案例研究。
  • Parents and Children Disagree Over Childhood Icons 家長與子女對童年標誌的分歧
    The split reaction, enthusiastic young fans against concerned parents, highlights how differently generations read the same cultural symbol: children see playful novelty, while parents see a cherished image being altered without their input. The disagreement says as much about shifting parenting expectations as it does about the park's creative choices.
    年輕粉絲的熱烈反應與家長的憂慮形成的分歧，顯示不同世代對同一文化符號有著截然不同的解讀：兒童看見的是有趣的新鮮感，家長看見的則是一個珍視的形象在未經他們同意下被改變。這種分歧所反映的，既是育兒期望的轉變，亦是樂園創作決定本身。
  • Who Decides How Children's Icons Should Look? 誰有權決定兒童標誌應有的形象？
    Because Disney princesses are marketed directly to young children, critics argue the company bears particular responsibility when altering their presentation for viral appeal, since children may absorb style cues uncritically. Supporters counter that updating choreography is a minor creative choice, but the ethical question of influence over impressionable audiences remains worth examining.
    由於迪士尼公主直接以年幼兒童為銷售對象，批評者認為公司在為追求爆紅效果而改動其形象時，須承擔特別的責任，因為兒童未必能批判地吸收這些風格提示。支持者則反駁，更新舞步只屬微小的創作決定，但對易受影響觀眾施加影響的道德問題，仍值得探討。
  • A Manufactured Controversy That Serves the Park 一場為樂園服務而製造的爭議
    It could be argued that the entire debate is a deliberate publicity tactic rather than a genuine cultural clash, since controversy itself generates exactly the engagement and visibility the park benefits from. Viewed this way, both the 'modernising' praise and the parental backlash may simply be two halves of the same marketing outcome.
    有人或會認為，整場爭論其實是刻意製造的宣傳手段，而非真正的文化衝突，因為爭議本身正正帶來樂園所得益的參與度及曝光率。按此角度看，無論是「與時並進」的讚賞，還是家長的反彈，都可能只是同一個市場推廣結果的兩面。

🧵 Threads' 'Pressure-Free Playground' Culture Takes Off in Hong Kong

Social Trend·6 Sep 2026
English

It is widely observed that Threads has seen explosive growthextremely rapid and sudden increase爆炸性增長 among Hong Kong users this year, driven largely by the city’s longstanding appetite for text-first, forum-style discussionconversation resembling an online discussion board論壇式討論. Local meme pages and lifestyle accounts have taken to describing the platform as a “pressure-free playground”, where users feel free to post spontaneouslywithout planning; on impulse自發地；即興地 without the polish demanded by Instagram. Because Threads’ algorithm is comparatively decentralisednot concentrated in the hands of a few powerful accounts去中心化的, even small accounts can spark a citywide reactiontrigger a sudden, widespread response引發全城反應, dubbed a “Threadquake”, giving ordinary users a rare sense that any post might go viralspread extremely quickly online爆紅 overnight. Commentators note that this shift matters in a city long associated with heavy social expectations around personal image, where a platform rewarding raw, unedited posts over curated perfection represents a genuinely unfamiliar way of being seen online.

中文翻譯

外界普遍觀察到，Threads今年在香港用戶間出現爆炸性增長，主要源於本地一直以來對以文字為主、論壇式討論的熱愛。本地迷因專頁及生活方式帳戶紛紛將這個平台形容為「無壓力遊樂場」，用戶可以自發地發帖，不必像在Instagram般講究精緻包裝。由於Threads的演算法相對去中心化，即使小帳戶亦有機會引發全城反應，被稱為「Threadquake」，讓普通用戶罕有地感受到任何一則貼文都有可能一夜爆紅。評論者指出，在一個長期重視個人形象、社會期望甚高的城市，一個獎勵未經修飾的真實貼文，而非精心編排的完美形象的平台，確實代表著一種前所未見的網上自我呈現方式。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • An Escape From Instagram's Curated Pressure 逃離Instagram的精緻包裝壓力
    By lowering the bar for polish and performance, Threads may ease the comparison anxiety long associated with heavily edited Instagram feeds. Writers could discuss whether a platform explicitly branded as 'pressure-free' genuinely improves users' wellbeing, or whether the relief is temporary until Threads itself develops its own unwritten rules of popularity.
    透過降低對精緻包裝及表演式經營的要求，Threads或許能緩解長期與高度修飾的Instagram動態掛鈎的比較焦慮。作家可探討一個明確標榜「無壓力」的平台是否真正改善用戶的身心健康，還是這種鬆一口氣的感覺只屬短暫，直至Threads自身發展出一套不成文的人氣規則。
  • A Decentralised Algorithm Lowers the Barrier to Virality 去中心化演算法降低爆紅門檻
    Unlike platforms dominated by established influencers, Threads' algorithm reportedly gives ordinary accounts a realistic chance of reaching a citywide audience. This democratising quality could be framed as improving access to public attention for users without existing followings, though it remains unclear how long such openness lasts before the platform matures and consolidates power among top creators.
    與由established網紅主導的平台不同，Threads的演算法據報讓普通帳戶有實際機會接觸全城觀眾。這種民主化的特質可被視為改善了沒有既有追蹤者的用戶獲得公眾關注的機會，但這種開放狀態能持續多久，直至平台成熟並將權力集中於頂尖創作者手中，仍屬未知。
  • Unfiltered Posting and the Risk of Oversharing 不經修飾的發帖與過度分享的風險
    The platform's casual, spontaneous posting culture may encourage users to share personal details or opinions without the usual filtering applied on more image-conscious platforms. This raises concerns about digital footprints and whether young users fully consider the permanence of posts made in an unguarded, low-pressure moment.
    平台隨意、自發的發帖文化，可能鼓勵用戶分享個人資料或意見，而未經其他重視形象的平台慣常採用的篩選。這引發關於數碼足跡的憂慮，以及年輕用戶是否充分考慮到，在一個缺乏防範、低壓力的時刻所發的貼文可能永久留存。
  • Just Another Platform Chasing Instagram's Fatigue 只是另一個乘Instagram疲態而起的平台
    Sceptics suggest Threads' appeal has less to do with genuine cultural shift and more to do with users simply growing tired of one platform and migrating to a newer one, a cycle that has repeated with every rival app for a decade. Under this view, the 'playground' framing is marketing spin rather than meaningful change.
    持懷疑態度者認為，Threads的吸引力與真正的文化轉變關係不大，反而更多源於用戶單純厭倦了一個平台，繼而轉投另一個較新的應用程式，這種循環在過去十年隨著每一個競爭對手應用程式出現而重演。按此觀點，「遊樂場」的描述只是市場推廣話術，而非具意義的轉變。

🕺 Feel Like Dance Challenge Brings 90s Disco Back to Hong Kong Malls

English

A wave of nostalgia-driven dance content has swept across Hong Kong social media under the bannera slogan or theme under which something is promoted旗號；口號 of the “Feel Like Dance Challenge”, timed to coincide with Hong Kong Disneyland’s 2026 celebrations. Participants recreateto make or produce something again重現 1990s-style disco moves set to a retroimitating a style from the past復古的 remixed soundtrack, often filmed in brightly lit public spaces such as shopping malls and MTR concourses. The trend has proven especially popular among secondary school and university students, who post side-by-side clips with parents or grandparents attempting the same choreography, tapping into a broader appetite for intergenerationalinvolving people from different generations跨代的 content on short-form video platforms. Brands have quickly moved to capitalise on the crazetake commercial advantage of a popular trend把握熱潮, with several retailers releasing themed merchandisebranded goods designed around a particular theme主題商品 and sponsoring dance workshops in shopping centres across the city.

中文翻譯

一股懷舊風格的跳舞短片熱潮席捲香港社交媒體，以「Feel Like Dance Challenge」為名，時機正好配合香港迪士尼樂園二零二六年的慶祝活動。參加者重現九十年代的士高舞步，配合復古混音金曲，拍攝地點多選於燈火通明的公共空間，例如商場及港鐵站大堂。這股潮流在中學及大學生之間尤其受歡迎，他們拍下與父母甚至祖父母一同跳同一套舞步的對比短片，呼應了短片平台上對跨代互動內容日漸增長的喜好。多個品牌亦迅速把握熱潮，推出主題商品，並於全港多個商場贊助跳舞工作坊。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • Bridging Generations Through Shared Choreography 透過共同舞步連繫兩代人
    By inviting parents and grandparents to attempt the same thirty-year-old dance steps as teenagers, the challenge creates a rare shared cultural reference point across generations. Writers could explore how such light-hearted formats build family bonding and mutual understanding in a city where generational communication gaps are often cited as a source of tension.
    透過邀請父母及祖父母嘗試與青少年相同的三十年前舞步，這項挑戰創造了一個罕有的跨代共同文化參照點。作家可藉此探討這類輕鬆的形式如何促進家庭聯繫及相互理解，尤其在一個常被指出存在代際溝通鴻溝的城市。
  • Retro Nostalgia as a Marketing Tool 復古懷舊成為市場推廣工具
    Hong Kong Disneyland and retailers were quick to attach themed merchandise and sponsored workshops to the trend, turning a spontaneous wave of nostalgia into a coordinated commercial campaign. This illustrates how corporations increasingly monitor organic youth trends in real time, ready to repackage them as promotional opportunities within days of going viral.
    香港迪士尼樂園及零售商迅速將主題商品及贊助工作坊附加於這股潮流之上，把一股自發的懷舊風潮變成一場有協調的商業推廣活動。這說明企業如今如何實時監察有機青年潮流，隨時準備在爆紅後數日內將其重新包裝為推廣機會。
  • Filming in Crowded Public Spaces 在擁擠公共空間拍攝的隱憂
    Shooting choreographed routines in busy malls and MTR concourses raises practical safety concerns, from blocking walkways to obstructing emergency exits during peak hours. Schools and venue operators may need to consider clearer guidance on where such filming is appropriate, balancing young people's enthusiasm for content creation against the public's right to move freely.
    在繁忙商場及港鐵站大堂拍攝編排舞步，引發實際的安全隱憂，由阻塞通道到在繁忙時段阻礙緊急出口皆有可能。學校及場地管理者或須就適合拍攝的地點訂立更清晰指引，在青少年對內容創作的熱情與公眾自由通行的權利之間取得平衡。
  • Nostalgia for a Decade Few Participants Lived Through 對一個大多參加者未曾經歷的年代的懷舊
    Critics might point out that most teenagers performing this '90s-inspired' routine were not even born in that decade, suggesting the nostalgia is manufactured rather than genuinely felt. This raises the question of whether such trends represent authentic cultural engagement or simply borrow an aesthetic because it photographs well and performs reliably online.
    批評者可能指出，大部分表演這套「九十年代風格」舞步的青少年根本未曾經歷那個年代，意味著這種懷舊情感是刻意營造而非真正感受到的。這引發一個問題：這類潮流究竟代表真正的文化參與，還是純粹因為某種風格拍起來好看、在網上表現可靠而被借用。

🧋 'Spritea' Craze: Hongkongers Are Dunking Tea Bags in Sprite

Social Trend·4 Sep 2026
English

A quirky drink hack has taken Hong Kong by storm: creators are dunkingdipping something briefly into liquid浸泡 ordinary tea bags directly into bottles of Sprite, producing a sweet, malty, citrus-laced concoctiona mixture of several ingredients混合飲品 dubbed “Spritea”. Having already gone viral in North America in 2025, the trend has now taken offbecome suddenly very popular迅速流行起來 among Hong Kong’s Gen Z social media users, with searches for the recipe surgingincreasing suddenly and sharply急升 by more than 200 per cent on TikTok within a single week. Local tea shops have reported a knock-on effectan indirect, secondary consequence of an event連鎖反應, as curious customers request the mash-up over the counter. Sensing an opportunity, Sprite moved to capitalise on the crazetake commercial advantage of a popular trend把握熱潮, launching an official ready-to-drink version and touring a mobile pop-up tea stall through high-traffic districts, handing out tens of thousands of free samples within days.

中文翻譯

一種古怪的飲品製作方法在香港掀起熱潮：創作者直接將普通茶包浸入雪碧樽內，調配出一種帶甜味、麥芽香及檸檬清香的混合飲品，被網民戲稱為「Spritea」。這股潮流早於二零二五年已在北美爆紅，如今亦在香港Z世代社交媒體用戶間迅速流行起來，短短一星期內，TikTok上相關食譜的搜尋量急升超過二百個百分點。本地茶飲店亦表示出現連鎖反應，不少好奇顧客要求店員現場調製這款混合飲品。雪碧品牌察覺到商機，隨即把握熱潮，推出官方即飲版本，並派出流動快閂店巡迴多個人流旺盛地區，數日內免費派發數萬份試飲裝。

DSE writing angles 寫作角度
  • From Viral Hack to Corporate Product 由病毒式秘技變成企業商品
    What began as an organic, user-invented drink hack was absorbed into official marketing within weeks, as Sprite launched its own ready-to-drink version and pop-up sampling tour. Students could examine how quickly brands co-opt youth-generated content, questioning whether such rapid commercialisation dilutes the spontaneity that made the trend appealing in the first place.
    一場原本自發、由用戶創造的飲品秘技，在短短數週內被納入官方市場推廣之中，因為雪碧推出了自家即飲版本及快閂試飲巡迴活動。學生可藉此探討品牌如何迅速收編青年自創內容，並反思這種快速商業化是否沖淡了令這股潮流一開始吸引人的那份自發性。
  • Lost Trade for Traditional Tea Shops 傳統茶飲店的生意流失
    While multinational brands profit from the craze, small independent tea shops selling authentic Hong Kong-style milk tea gain little, since the trend celebrates a soda-brand mashup rather than local tea culture. This raises questions about whether viral trends genuinely support small local businesses or mainly benefit corporations with marketing budgets to exploit them.
    儘管跨國品牌從這股熱潮中獲利，售賣正宗港式奶茶的小型獨立茶檜卻幾乎未能分一杯羹，因為這股潮流慶祝的是汽水與茶的混搭，而非本地茶文化本身。這引發一個問題：病毒式潮流究竟是真正扶助本地小商戶，還是主要讓擁有雄厚推廣預算的大企業得益。
  • Sugar and Caffeine Risks Behind the Novelty 新奇感背後的糖分與咖啡因風險
    Mixing sugary soda with caffeinated tea significantly raises the sugar and caffeine content of a single drink, a concern nutritionists have flagged as the trend spreads among students who may not consider the cumulative health impact of repeatedly recreating the recipe simply to stay part of an online moment.
    將含糖汽水與含咖啡因的茶混合，大幅提高單一飲品的糖分及咖啡因含量，這是營養師提出的隱憂，尤其當這股潮流在學生之間傳播，他們未必會考慮到為了跟上網上熱潮而反覆調製這款飲品所帶來的累積健康影響。
  • A Fad With No Lasting Value 一股缺乏持久價值的風潮
    Sceptics argue that Spritea says little meaningful about Hong Kong youth culture at all, calling it simply an imported gimmick recycled for clicks, destined to be forgotten within months like countless other drink mashups, and therefore undeserving of the sustained media attention and brand investment it has received.
    持懷疑態度者認為，Spritea其實無法反映香港青年文化的任何深層意義，只是一股從外地搬字過紙、純為搏取點擊率而循環再造的噱頭，終將如無數其他飲品混搭一樣，在數月內被人遺忘，因此不值得媒體及品牌投放如此多的持續關注與資源。
📖 Study Notes ▾
Key Vocabulary
1 drink hack
飲品製作秘技
"The drink hack of mixing tea with soda spread quickly among teenagers online."
2 malty
帶麥芽味的
"The tea bags gave the fizzy drink a surprisingly malty aftertaste."
3 citrus-laced
帶有柑橘味的
"The citrus-laced soda paired unexpectedly well with the steeped tea."
4 ready-to-drink
即飲裝
"The brand rushed out a ready-to-drink version once the hack went viral."
5 pop-up stall
快閂店；臨時攤位
"A pop-up stall handed out free samples of the new flavour in Causeway Bay."
6 high-traffic district
人流旺盛地區
"The company chose a high-traffic district to maximise exposure for its giveaway."
7 mash-up
混搭組合
"The soda-and-tea mash-up quickly became a talking point among students."
8 co-opt
挪用；收編
"Large companies often co-opt grassroots internet trends for their own marketing."
9 grassroots trend
草根潮流
"What started as a grassroots trend was turned into a branded product within weeks."
10 fizzy drink
汽水
"Nutritionists warned that mixing a fizzy drink with caffeinated tea adds up quickly."
Quick Reference — Phrases & Sample Sentences
Phrase / Expression釋義DSE Sample Sentence
spread like wildfire online 在網上迅速蔓延 The soda-and-tea recipe spread like wildfire online within days of the first clip.
blur the line between hack and product 模糊了自製秘技與商品之間的界線 Sprite’s swift launch blurred the line between a homemade hack and an official product.
ride the wave of a trend 乘著潮流的浪頭 The brand rode the wave of the trend before public interest had a chance to fade.
repackage a grassroots idea 將草根創意重新包裝 Critics accused the company of repackaging a grassroots idea purely for profit.
cash in on online buzz 藉網上熱議獲利 Several beverage brands have tried to cash in on online buzz surrounding food mash-ups.
fuel a surge in demand 推動需求急升 Viral clips of the drink fuelled a surge in demand for tea bags among teenagers.
overlook the health implications 忽視健康影響 Fans of the trend may overlook the health implications of combining sugar and caffeine.
reward corporate speed over originality 獎勵企業的速度而非原創性 The episode shows how viral culture can reward corporate speed over originality.
leave original creators uncredited 令原創者未獲認可 The rapid commercialisation left the trend’s original creators uncredited and uncompensated.
